## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

- codebase-memory: Use the codebase knowledge graph for structural code queries. Triggers on: explore the codebase, understand the architecture, what functions exist, show me the structure, who calls this function, what does X call, trace the call chain, find callers of, show dependencies, impact analysis, dead code, unused functions, high fan-out, refactor candidates, code quality audit, graph query syntax, Cypher query examples, edge types, how to use search_graph.
- commit: Commit pending changes split into logical change sets, each with a Conventional Commits message prefixed by a relevant emoji. Use when the user asks to commit, group/stage changes into logical commits, or write conventional-commit messages with emoji (gitmoji-style).
- development-docs: Decide whether anything from the current session belongs in docs/DEVELOPMENT.md (recurring dev patterns) or docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md (bugs/gotchas), and record it with a cited source if so. Use before finalizing a commit (invoked as a step of the commit skill, and reminded by a pre-commit hook), or when the user explicitly asks to record a pattern, gotcha, or lesson learned.
- frontend-design:frontend-design: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
- council:council: Convene the Council of High Intelligence — multi-persona deliberation with historical thinkers for deeper analysis of complex problems.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 1: capture


def prepare_capture(
    config: WorkspaceConfig,
    kind: str,
    client: ModelClient,
    *,
    file: Path | None = None,
    url: str | None = None,
    context: str | None = None,
    context_digest: str | None = None,
    context_referenced_paths: list[str] | None = None,
) -> CaptureProposal:
    meeting_date: str | None = None
    if kind in ("transcript", "text"):
        if file is None:
            raise IngestError(f"{kind} ingest needs a file path")
        if kind == "transcript" and file.suffix.lower() == ".whisper":
            text, recorded_at = parse_whisper_transcript(file)
            meeting_date = infer_meeting_date(file, text) or recorded_at
        else:
            try:
                raw = file.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
            except OSError as exc:
                raise IngestError(f"Could not read {file}: {exc}") from exc
            text = strip_srt(raw) if file.suffix.lower() == ".srt" else raw
            if kind == "transcript":
                text = clean_transcript(text)
                meeting_date = infer_meeting_date(file, text)
        origin = _relative_origin(config, file)
        stem = _LEADING_DATE_RE.sub("", file.stem) or file.stem
        # Deterministic basis for the raw file's slug only -- see below,
        # this is intentionally never overwritten by the model's title.
        slug_source = stem.replace("-", " ").replace("_", " ").strip() or file.name
    elif kind == "article":
        if url is None:
            raise IngestError("article ingest needs a URL")
        article = fetch_article(url)
        text = article.text
        origin = url
        slug_source = article.title
    else:
        raise IngestError(f"unknown ingest kind: {kind}")

    if not text.strip():
        raise IngestError("Source contains no text")

    content_hash = hashlib.sha256(text.encode()).hexdigest()
    proposal = CaptureProposal(
        source_type=kind,
        origin=origin,
        title=slug_source,
        text=text,
        content_hash=content_hash,
        context=context,
        context_digest=context_digest,
        context_referenced_paths=list(context_referenced_paths or []),
        meeting_date=meeting_date,
        raw_file=ProposedFile(path="", content=""),
    )

    with open_session(config) as session:
        existing = session.scalar(select(Source.id).where(Source.content_hash == content_hash))
        if existing is not None:
            proposal.duplicate_of = existing
            return proposal

Found it. `wakil` does have a diarization-aware transcript parser — `parse_whisper_transcript()` in `ingest_service.py:1448` — but it's gated on the file being a `.whisper` **zip archive** (Apple's Whisper Transcription app format: `metadata.json` inside a zip, with a `transcripts` array where each segment's speaker is `{"name": ...}`). Your file is a plain `.json` with a `segments` array and a flat `"speaker": "Speaker 1"` string — a different tool's export shape entirely. Since the extension check (`file.suffix.lower() == ".whisper"`) failed, ingestion fell through to the generic branch (`ingest_service.py:243-250`), which only does regex-based `clean_transcript()` (timestamp/whitespace stripping) on raw text — it has no JSON awareness at all, so the whole JSON blob passed through as "text."

So it's not that wakil chose not to diarize — it just doesn't yet recognize this JSON schema as a transcript format. Two options if you want diarized output for this source: (1) add a second parser branch keyed on the `segments`/flat-speaker shape (mirrors `parse_whisper_transcript` but without the zip/`.whisper`-specific bits), or (2) if this is a one-off, hand-convert the file. Given wakil's bias toward small, explicit handling per known format rather than a generic transcript-format registry, option 1 fits — but only worth it if you expect more transcripts from this same source going forward. Want me to look at what tool produced this JSON and sketch that parser?

"""Ingest raw sources into the knowledge base — in two separate steps.

Step 1, capture (`wakil ingest ...`): deterministic except for one small
model call (docs/adr/0010-capture-time-title-and-abstract-generation.md).
The source text is extracted (transcripts get light cleanup), deduped by
content hash, and written under sources/ as a raw capture with frontmatter
shaped by the `source` entity schema's base fields plus its `transcript`
origin sub-schema (`schema/entities/source.yaml`) — the schema catalog, not
a workspace-authored template, is the source of truth for this shape. The
raw file's path/slug stays fully deterministic (derived from the
filename/article scrape, never the model); only the frontmatter
`title:`/`abstract:` content comes from the model, via a single cheap call
against the `CaptureMetadata` contract.

Step 2, enrichment (`wakil enrich <source-id>`): a fixed, code-sequenced DAG
(docs/ingestion-refactor-spec.md) — an extraction model call (judgment from
the `<kind>` skill against the ExtractionOutput contract), then an
always-invoked entity-resolution model call (the `entity-resolve` skill
against EntityResolution), then `validate_proposal()` gating every proposed
new file against the entity schemas, then one preview/confirm, then apply.
Both skills are resolved through `wakil.skills.resolver` (built-in by
default, kb-local/user overridable) via `wakil.llm.skill_loader.load_skill`.

Each step is itself two-phase (prepare → preview/confirm → apply): prepare
touches nothing, files are only ever created (never overwritten), and DB rows
are only written in apply, so declining a preview leaves no trace.
"""

import contextlib
import hashlib
import json
import re
import zipfile
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import UTC, date, datetime, timedelta
from pathlib import Path

import frontmatter as frontmatter_lib
import yaml
from sqlalchemy import or_, select

    """Extract speaker-labeled dialogue from an Apple-style .whisper archive.

    A `.whisper` file is a zip containing `metadata.json`: diarized
    `transcripts` segments (speaker name, start/end ms, text) plus a
    `speakers` roster and capture timestamps. Consecutive segments from the
    same speaker are merged into one turn, and standalone ASR filler tokens
    are stripped (see `_strip_filler_words`) — otherwise the text is kept
    verbatim.

    Returns (dialogue_text, recorded_at) where recorded_at is an ISO date
    derived from the archive's own capture timestamp, or None if absent.
    """
    data = _read_whisper_metadata(file)
    segments = data.get("transcripts")
    if not isinstance(segments, list) or not segments:
        raise IngestError(f"{file}: metadata.json has no transcript segments")

    turns: list[tuple[str, list[str]]] = []
    for segment in sorted(segments, key=lambda s: s.get("start", 0)):
        text = _strip_filler_words(str(segment.get("text", "")).strip())
        if not text:

        speaker = str((segment.get("speaker") or {}).get("name") or "").strip() or "Unknown speaker"

            turns[-1][1].append(text)

| | `.whisper` archive | your `.json` |
|---|---|---|
| container | zip w/ `metadata.json` inside | plain JSON file |
| top-level key | `transcripts` | `segments` |
| speaker field | `{"name": "Speaker 1", "id": ..., "color": ...}` | `"Speaker 1"` (flat string) |
| capture timestamp | `dateCreated` (Apple epoch) | none |

**Fix applied** (`src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`):
- Factored the segment→dialogue merge logic (consecutive-same-speaker merging, filler-word stripping) out of `parse_whisper_transcript` into a shared `_dialogue_from_segments()` helper.

# development-docs

Keep `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` and `docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md` high-signal. The default,
expected outcome of running this skill is **no change to either file** — most
sessions produce nothing worth recording. Padding these files to "have something
to show" is a violation of their purpose.

## When to use

- As a step inside the `commit` skill's procedure, before finalizing commits.
- When reminded by the pre-commit hook.
- When the user explicitly says something like "note this gotcha", "add this
  pattern to the dev docs", or "record this for next time".

## Procedure

1. **Review what happened.** Look at the session's diff and the problem(s) actually
   solved — not what was attempted or discussed, only what landed.
2. **Apply the bar** (below) to each candidate. Be skeptical by default: if you're
   unsure whether it clears the bar, it doesn't.
3. **If something clears the bar**, write a dated entry in the format below, citing
   a concrete source. Include the doc edit as part of the commit's change sets
   rather than a separate follow-up.
4. **If nothing clears the bar**, do nothing. Don't note that you "considered and
   rejected" anything — just proceed.

## Bar for inclusion

- **`docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md`** — a bug or gotcha that (a) cost real debugging
  time, (b) wasn't obvious from reading the code, and (c) would plausibly recur or
  mislead someone again.
- **`docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`** — a pattern that was established or reinforced that
  should generalize to *future, different* work — not a one-off fix specific to
  this change.
- **Default: no entry.**

## Entry format

`docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md`:

```markdown
### <short, specific title>
**Date:** YYYY-MM-DD · **Source:** <commit SHA / PR # / brief pointer>

<2-5 sentences: symptom, root cause, fix or workaround.>
```

`docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`:

```markdown
### <pattern name>
**Established:** YYYY-MM-DD · **Source:** <commit SHA / PR # / brief pointer>

<2-5 sentences: what the pattern is, when to apply it, where else it's used.>
```

## Rules

- Every entry must cite a concrete source (commit SHA, PR #, or a specific, checkable
  detail) — no vague or unattributed claims.
- Keep entries short: 2-5 sentences. Link to the relevant code or doc rather than
  duplicating it.
- Append only. Never rewrite or delete an existing entry without the user's
  explicit go-ahead.

---
title: Development Patterns
status: living
audience: wakil design
---

# Development Patterns

Recurring dev conventions worth generalizing to future, different work — not
a changelog and not a place for one-off fixes. An entry only belongs here if
the pattern should apply beyond the change that established it. Most work
sessions should add nothing; see the `development-docs` skill
(`.claude/skills/development-docs/SKILL.md`) for the judgment process that maintains
this file. Every entry cites a concrete source (commit SHA, PR #, or session
detail) for traceability.

### Split error handling around a git-landing step
**Source:** PR #15 (`worktree-git-integration` branch), `src/wakil/cli/main.py`

When a command lands on a branch (`prepare_landing`) before doing risked work (e.g. `apply_capture`/`apply_enrichment`), catch the landing call's `GitServiceError` in its own `try` block, separate from the subsequent operation's errors. On any failure in the operation after a successful landing, call `abandon_landing(config, landing)` so the worktree returns to its own branch instead of being left stranded on the throwaway ingest branch. `enrich` established this shape first (commit `f5a4ed1`); `_run_ingest` originally wrapped `prepare_landing` and `apply_capture` in one combined `try` block, and was split to match `enrich` in commit `a14af48`, whose message describes closing the gap this way: "so a race loss returns the session to its original branch via abandon_landing instead of stranding it on the throwaway ingest branch."

Note: as of this writing PR #15 is still an open draft (unmerged into `main`); this pattern applies once/if that branch lands.

### Run the live eval before treating new SKILL.md guidance as done
**Source:** PR #20 (`docs/skill-guidance-for-linked-context` branch), `src/wakil/skills/entity-enrichment/SKILL.md`

Adding a new rule to a skill's SKILL.md and a matching `eval.json` scenario for it isn't finished until `uv run pytest -m eval -k <scenario id>` (a real model call, per `docs/adr/0004`) actually passes — prose that reads correct to a human reviewer can still be misapplied by the model in a way only a live run surfaces. Here, a new rule said an explicit `@file:` reference should be treated as "high-confidence" for back-linking; the model read that confidence as also covering content-worthiness and appended a Timeline entry for a mention the source said had nothing new to report, failing the eval's rubric. The fix was one clarifying sentence separating the link decision from the content decision — but the gap was invisible without actually running the eval. When adding or editing skill guidance, write (or extend) its `eval.json` scenario and run it live before considering the change done, not just at merge/CI time.

### A skill's `references/*.md` files are never loaded into the model's context
**Source:** `fix/eval-suite-flakiness-and-skill-gaps` branch, live-eval triage session, 2026-07-21

`load_skill()` (`src/wakil/llm/skill_loader.py`) builds `skill.body` from `SKILL.md` alone — nothing inlines a skill's `references/*.md` files, even though several SKILL.md files (`source-ingestion`, `skill-authoring`) point at them for what reads as load-bearing judgment ("see `references/source-types.md` for the per-source-type judgment"). This is true both in `wakil enrich`'s real pipeline (`build_system_prompt`) and the eval harness (`run_scenario`) — a human reading the skill file would follow the pointer and find the guidance; the model never does, regardless of how clearly SKILL.md cites the file. Two separate live-eval failures (a fabricated YouTube-transcription workaround, a promotion checklist the model never applied) traced to this exact cause. When a SKILL.md cites a `references/` file for guidance that actually needs to affect model behavior (not just serve as a longer human-readable writeup), pull the load-bearing part into `SKILL.md`'s own body — `references/` can still carry the fuller version, but the file itself must not be the only place the instruction lives.

### Check whether a skill's own procedure step order can produce the bug it's trying to prevent
**Source:** `fix/eval-suite-flakiness-and-skill-gaps` branch, `note-routing/SKILL.md`, 2026-07-21

`note-routing`'s decision tree had "generate the filename" as Step 5 and "surface ambiguity, don't pick" as Step 6 — so a model following the numbered steps in order committed to a filename before ever reaching the ambiguity check the later step was supposed to gate. The instruction to "surface ambiguity" was correct in isolation; the bug was purely in where it sat relative to the step it needed to precede. When a skill's procedure is a numbered sequence and a later step is meant to be a conditional gate on an earlier one, check that the gate actually comes first — a correct rule stated too late in the list doesn't prevent the thing it names.

### Print diagnostic detail as it happens, not deferred to a final summary

ADR 0006 ("Backlinks as a Live Query Over a Widened Relationship Table") is `status: accepted` and its schema/migration exist, but grepping the real application code turned up exactly one place a `Relationship` row is ever constructed (`ingest_service.py`'s `apply_enrichment`) — and it only ever writes `subject_memory_id`/`object_memory_id`. The note-note columns the ADR is about (`subject_note_id`/`object_note_id`) are populated nowhere in the real pipeline, exercised only by one hand-constructed unit test roundtrip. This wasn't caught until a downstream consumer (a kb-side skill assuming backlinks were already automatic) went looking for the actual write path. Before citing an accepted ADR's decision as current, working behavior in a new design doc, a docstring, or downstream documentation, grep for where it's actually implemented — `status: accepted` records that a decision was made, not that every consequence of it landed in code.

+### Diarized transcript formats each get their own `parse_<x>_transcript()` sharing one merge helper

+A plain-JSON transcript export (`{"segments": [{"speaker": "Speaker 1", "text": ..., "start": ...}]}`) looked like the same shape as an Apple `.whisper` zip archive's `metadata.json` (`{"transcripts": [{"speaker": {"name": ...}, ...}]}`) but wasn't — different container (zip vs. plain file), different top-level key (`transcripts` vs. `segments`), different speaker shape (object vs. flat string) — so it fell through `prepare_capture`'s generic text branch and captured as a raw, undiarized JSON blob instead of dialogue. The fix factored the actual merge logic (consecutive-same-speaker turns, filler-word stripping) out of `parse_whisper_transcript` into a shared `_dialogue_from_segments(segments, speaker_of)` helper, then added `parse_json_transcript()` as a second, format-specific caller. The next new diarized export shape (a different ASR tool's JSON, an SRT-with-speaker-labels variant, etc.) should follow the same shape: a small `parse_<x>_transcript()` that extracts its own `segments` list and a `speaker_of` callable, gated on file suffix/content in `prepare_capture`, reusing `_dialogue_from_segments` rather than re-implementing the merge.

draft a plan for a mechanism that will periodically "compress" entities so that they don't contribute to API ModelTruncationErrors as an upstream tactic to further prevent overloading the context when enriching entities.

Some general guidance: older entries are less interesting than more recent entries. "Compiled Truth" should be built on important facts, it should be derived from the timeline.  timelines are very important and should remain intact, though more detail in older entries is less interesting -- the important stuff should be concisely integrated into the "Compiled Truth".  The timeline should not be included in context -- just the "Compiled Truth", since the most important information has already found its way into the Compiled Truth.

1	---
2	title: Development Patterns
3	status: living
4	audience: wakil design
5	---
6	
7	# Development Patterns
8	
9	Recurring dev conventions worth generalizing to future, different work — not
10	a changelog and not a place for one-off fixes. An entry only belongs here if
11	the pattern should apply beyond the change that established it. Most work
12	sessions should add nothing; see the `development-docs` skill
13	(`.claude/skills/development-docs/SKILL.md`) for the judgment process that maintains
14	this file. Every entry cites a concrete source (commit SHA, PR #, or session
15	detail) for traceability.
16	
17	### Split error handling around a git-landing step
18	**Source:** PR #15 (`worktree-git-integration` branch), `src/wakil/cli/main.py`
19	
20	When a command lands on a branch (`prepare_landing`) before doing risked work (e.g. `apply_capture`/`apply_enrichment`), catch the landing call's `GitServiceError` in its own `try` block, separate from the subsequent operation's errors. On any failure in the operation after a successful landing, call `abandon_landing(config, landing)` so the worktree returns to its own branch instead of being left stranded on the throwaway ingest branch. `enrich` established this shape first (commit `f5a4ed1`); `_run_ingest` originally wrapped `prepare_landing` and `apply_capture` in one combined `try` block, and was split to match `enrich` in commit `a14af48`, whose message describes closing the gap this way: "so a race loss returns the session to its original branch via abandon_landing instead of stranding it on the throwaway ingest branch."
21	
22	Note: as of this writing PR #15 is still an open draft (unmerged into `main`); this pattern applies once/if that branch lands.
23	
24	### Run the live eval before treating new SKILL.md guidance as done
25	**Source:** PR #20 (`docs/skill-guidance-for-linked-context` branch), `src/wakil/skills/entity-enrichment/SKILL.md`
26	
27	Adding a new rule to a skill's SKILL.md and a matching `eval.json` scenario for it isn't finished until `uv run pytest -m eval -k <scenario id>` (a real model call, per `docs/adr/0004`) actually passes — prose that reads correct to a human reviewer can still be misapplied by the model in a way only a live run surfaces. Here, a new rule said an explicit `@file:` reference should be treated as "high-confidence" for back-linking; the model read that confidence as also covering content-worthiness and appended a Timeline entry for a mention the source said had nothing new to report, failing the eval's rubric. The fix was one clarifying sentence separating the link decision from the content decision — but the gap was invisible without actually running the eval. When adding or editing skill guidance, write (or extend) its `eval.json` scenario and run it live before considering the change done, not just at merge/CI time.
28	
29	### A skill's `references/*.md` files are never loaded into the model's context
30	**Source:** `fix/eval-suite-flakiness-and-skill-gaps` branch, live-eval triage session, 2026-07-21
31	
32	`load_skill()` (`src/wakil/llm/skill_loader.py`) builds `skill.body` from `SKILL.md` alone — nothing inlines a skill's `references/*.md` files, even though several SKILL.md files (`source-ingestion`, `skill-authoring`) point at them for what reads as load-bearing judgment ("see `references/source-types.md` for the per-source-type judgment"). This is true both in `wakil enrich`'s real pipeline (`build_system_prompt`) and the eval harness (`run_scenario`) — a human reading the skill file would follow the pointer and find the guidance; the model never does, regardless of how clearly SKILL.md cites the file. Two separate live-eval failures (a fabricated YouTube-transcription workaround, a promotion checklist the model never applied) traced to this exact cause. When a SKILL.md cites a `references/` file for guidance that actually needs to affect model behavior (not just serve as a longer human-readable writeup), pull the load-bearing part into `SKILL.md`'s own body — `references/` can still carry the fuller version, but the file itself must not be the only place the instruction lives.
33	
34	### Check whether a skill's own procedure step order can produce the bug it's trying to prevent
35	**Source:** `fix/eval-suite-flakiness-and-skill-gaps` branch, `note-routing/SKILL.md`, 2026-07-21
36	
37	`note-routing`'s decision tree had "generate the filename" as Step 5 and "surface ambiguity, don't pick" as Step 6 — so a model following the numbered steps in order committed to a filename before ever reaching the ambiguity check the later step was supposed to gate. The instruction to "surface ambiguity" was correct in isolation; the bug was purely in where it sat relative to the step it needed to precede. When a skill's procedure is a numbered sequence and a later step is meant to be a conditional gate on an earlier one, check that the gate actually comes first — a correct rule stated too late in the list doesn't prevent the thing it names.
38	
39	### Print diagnostic detail as it happens, not deferred to a final summary
40	**Source:** `fix/eval-suite-flakiness-and-skill-gaps` branch, `scripts/classify_eval_failures.py` and `uv run pytest -m eval -v` runs, 2026-07-21/22
41	
42	Two separate long-running eval scripts in this session lost their most important output to the same mistake: accumulating results in memory and only printing the useful summary (pytest's failure list, this script's per-item failure reasons) at the very end of the run. `scripts/classify_eval_failures.py` hit a live-model API usage cap partway through a 10-scenario classification pass and crashed — the log had per-scenario pass/fail counts but none of the actual failing rubric items or grader reasons, because those were only assembled into the final `CLASSIFICATION TABLE` the crash never reached. Fixed by printing each individual grading result (pass/fail, failed item, grader reason) immediately as it happens, keeping the end-of-run table as a convenience recap rather than the only place the detail lives. For any script making a sequence of live model calls with real cost/failure risk, print the thing you'd actually need to read *at the point each result arrives*, not after the loop — a partial run should still be a useful run.
43	
44	### Zip a vendored data file, document its source in a sibling `.SOURCE.md`
45	**Source:** PR #21 (`refactor/candidate-notes-stopword-filtering` branch), `src/wakil/app/data/`
46	
47	When vendoring a third-party data file (a word list, a static lookup table) into the repo, zip it rather than committing plain text — `common_words.zip` is 17KB against the original 34KB `common_words.txt`, decompressed once at import time via the stdlib `zipfile` module, not re-read per call. Because a zip's contents aren't reviewable in a plain `git diff`, add a sibling `<name>.SOURCE.md` documenting where the data came from, its license, and how to regenerate/refresh it — `common_words.SOURCE.md` is the template to copy for the next one.
48	
49	### A full live-model eval-suite run has a high baseline failure rate — don't read it as a regression signal
50	**Source:** session comparing `uv run pytest -m eval -q` across PRs #21-#24 and `main`, 2026-07-21

I have sufficient material. Let me write up the comprehensive research report.

## Research report: entity compression mechanism for `wakil enrich`

### 1. The full `wakil enrich <source-id>` pipeline, step by step

**Entry point:** `src/wakil/cli/main.py:504-613` (`enrich` command). Two-phase: `prepare_enrichment` (touches nothing) → preview/confirm → `apply_enrichment` (writes). Before either runs, `prepare_landing` (`src/wakil/app/git_service.py:132-163`) switches onto the source's per-source branch (creating it if new).

**`prepare_enrichment`** — `src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py:550-684`:

1. **Load source + related notes** (lines 559-630). Loads `Source` row, refuses re-enrichment unless `--force`. Builds `related_notes`: first the `@file:`-referenced notes (guaranteed, unranked), then top-`RELATED_NOTE_LIMIT=5` (line 83) FTS/QMD hits from `search_workspace`, then a direct proper-noun/title lookup against entity directories (`_candidate_entity_notes`, lines 772-816) to catch short entity stubs that lose to longer notes in relevance ranking.
2. **DAG node 1 — extraction call** (`_run_extraction`, lines 819-854, invoked at line 643). Loads the `<source_type>` skill (falls back to `text`) via `wakil.skills.resolver`/`load_skill`. System prompt = skill + `ExtractionOutput` contract (`build_system_prompt`). User prompt built by `build_extraction_prompt` (`llm/prompts.py`) from: source text truncated to `MAX_SOURCE_CHARS=24_000` chars (line 82, 637), `related_pairs` (path/title), the entity-schema catalog + page-shape templates, `context`, and `guides` (RESOLVER.md excerpt, `GUIDE_MAX_CHARS=4_000`, line 84). Populates `proposal.summary`, `key_points`, `memories` (→ `CandidateMemory`), `relationships`, and optionally `proposed_note`.
3. **DAG node 2 — entity resolution call, always invoked** (`_run_entity_resolution`, lines 857-885, invoked at line 683). Loads the `entity-resolve` skill (note: **not** the `entity-resolution/` directory — that's a separate, apparently-superseded skill dir; the code loads `"entity-resolve"`, `src/wakil/skills/entity-resolve/SKILL.md`). System = skill + `EntityResolutionOutput`. Prompt via `build_resolution_prompt`: source text, `proposal.summary`, the proposed note's markdown (if any), `related_pairs`, entity schemas, context, guides. On `ModelContractError`, degrades to a `proposal.warnings` entry and returns (no exception raised — entity resolution failure doesn't block create/stub write path). On success:
   - `_build_stub_entities` (888-930): one schema-valid stub page per `action="create"` resolution, skeleton = `_stub_content` (1244-1255): `## Compiled Truth` / `## Open Threads` / `---` / `## Timeline / Log`.
   - `_reconcile_entity_links` (947-1006): corrects `proposed_note`'s wikilinks to match entity-resolution's authoritative path (deterministic string rewrite, never a model call; logged to `warnings`).
   - `_run_entity_updates` → **DAG node 3**.
4. **DAG node 3 — entity revision call(s)** (`_run_entity_updates`, 1100-1148, and `_revise_candidates`, 1203-1241). For every `action="update"` resolution whose target's schema has `page_shape == "compiled-truth-timeline"`: filters out `relevance in {"minor", "peripheral"}` (line 1091, 1117-1119, ADR 0015 Decision 1) — surfaced as one `warnings` entry ("N entities left untouched as below the relevance threshold"), reads each target file's full current content. Remaining `candidates` go to `_revise_candidates`: loads `note-revision` skill, system = skill + `EntityRevisionOutput`, prompt via `build_revision_prompt(text, proposal.summary, targets, context)` which returns `(cacheable_prefix, variable_suffix)` — prefix = context + summary + full source text (stable, marked for prompt caching); suffix = per-target instructions + each target's **full existing content** inlined (`llm/prompts.py:175-226`). One call for the whole candidate batch. **On `ModelTruncatedError`** (after `complete_with_contract`'s own doubling retry, 8192→16384 tokens, `llm/schemas.py:200-213`): bisects the candidate list by existing-note content length (`_split_candidates_by_content_length`, greedy longest-first 2-way balance, 1151-1171) and recurses, up to `_MAX_BISECTION_DEPTH=3` (line 1095, ≤8 sub-batches). A non-truncation `ModelContractError` never triggers a split. Results merged deterministically by `_apply_entity_revisions` (1174-1200) → `_merge_entity_note` (1041-1085): surgical merge — H1 line preserved verbatim, everything between H1 and `## Timeline / Log` (accepts bare `## Timeline` too, line 1021) replaced by the re-synthesized `compiled_truth` (empty/absent means "no change," never "delete," line 1074-1079), one new dated entry prepended into Timeline (`_insert_timeline_entry`, 1024-1035), frontmatter merged (`frontmatter_updates`) with `updated:` stamped to today. Returns `None` (skip, warn) if the note doesn't match the expected H1+Timeline shape.

**`validate_proposal`** (1258-1337) — hard gate between prepare and apply: every proposed new file's frontmatter must validate against its entity schema; every `entity_updates` merged file re-validated too; unknown/directory-less create types are hard stops.

**`apply_enrichment`** (1340-1450):
1. Re-runs `validate_proposal`; raises (writes nothing) on any issue.
2. Writes `proposed_note` + `stub_entities` (refuses to overwrite existing files).
3. For each `entity_updates` item: **re-reads the target file immediately before writing** and skips (records in `stale_updates_skipped`, doesn't crash) any file whose content differs from `EntityUpdate.old_content` captured at prepare time — mirrors `schema_migrate_service`'s stale-file guard.
4. Writes `Memory` rows (`state="candidate"` always) and `Relationship` rows to the DB, flips `Source.status = "enriched"`, records an `IngestRun`, re-indexes notes.

Back in the CLI, `_land_written_files` → `land_ingestion` (`git_service.py:175-225`) commits exactly the written files onto the source's branch, flips its PR draft→ready, posts a phase comment.

### 2. The `entity-enrichment` skill

`src/wakil/skills/entity-enrichment/SKILL.md`. **Important finding: this skill is not invoked anywhere in the code DAG.** It explicitly documents that the CLI stops short of it:

> "That's identity resolution and page scaffolding, not enrichment. The CLI path does not decide which of the source's *other* mentions deserve a back-link, does not write anything into State (Compiled Truth), and does not add Timeline entries beyond what extraction directly proposed. That judgment is this skill's job — applied to a freshly-stubbed page, an existing page being updated with new signal, or a mention encountered during `note-revision` or manual editing, anywhere outside the CLI's fixed DAG."

The verbatim judgment guidance on Compiled Truth vs Timeline (which mirrors, and cross-references, `note-revision/SKILL.md`):

> "**Texture over facts** — A page's Compiled Truth should read like an intelligence dossier, not a scraped fact sheet... When updating an existing page, re-synthesize Compiled Truth to cover the union of what was already known plus the new signal — never replace it with only what the newest source said, and treat 'my rewritten section is shorter than what was there' as a stop-and-check signal, not confirmation you're done. Timeline entries are append-only: add dated entries, never delete or reorder what's already there, including auto-generated back-link lines."

> "**Scale effort to importance** — Not every entity deserves the same investment... effort is a dial, not a fixed procedure."

The DAG's actual model call for Compiled Truth/Timeline updates runs on the **`note-revision`** skill (`src/wakil/skills/note-revision/SKILL.md`), which is the one that matters for compression since it's the skill actually loaded by `_revise_candidates`. Its core discipline, verbatim:

> "**State (Compiled Truth)** is *re-synthesized* on every update to cover the union of what was already there plus the new facts... **Timeline (Log)** is *append-only*. New dated entries are added; existing entries — including auto-generated back-link lines — are never deleted, rewritten, or reordered. Losing a previously synthesized fact is a regression, not an update."

And its named failure mode, "the clobbering bug":

> "Prefer surgical edits — append a Timeline entry, edit the State block — over rewriting an existing page wholesale. Treat 'my new version is shorter than the old one' as a stop-and-check signal, not something to wave through."

This is directly in tension with what a compression mechanism must do (deliberately shrink content) — any compression design needs an explicit, separate code path/skill that is allowed to shrink Compiled Truth/Timeline, since both `note-revision` and `entity-enrichment` treat shrinkage as a red flag by design.

### 3. Database schema for Memory / Relationship / Note / Source

`src/wakil/storage/schema.py`. Relevant `Memory` columns (lines 82-113):
```
memory_type: String(30)   # free-string: fact|opinion|summary|relationship|question|hypothesis|decision|theme|event
content: Text
confidence: float | None  # 0.0-1.0, identity/certainty-ish signal (ADR 0013)
stance: String(10) | None # "formal"|"casual" — commitment/register axis (ADR 0014); NOT "register" at ORM level (Pydantic ABCMeta collision)
state: String(20) = "working"   # actually always "candidate" at write time per apply_enrichment; promote/reject/archive move it
importance: float | None  # column exists but nothing in ingest_service.py writes it
freshness: float | None   # column exists but nothing in ingest_service.py writes it
event_date: date | None   # the described event's own date, for Timeline ordering
last_seen_at: datetime | None
created_at / updated_at
```
`Note` (67-79) has `path`, `title`, `frontmatter_json`, `content_hash`, `last_indexed_at` — no register/importance columns; entity pages' "importance" lives only in the markdown (frontmatter/content), not the DB. `Source`/`Relationship`/`IngestRun` as expected; no schema field distinguishes old vs. new content within a note.

**ADR 0013** (opinion type + confidence-as-ranking): confidence became a `search_memories`/`retrieval_rank` tiebreak only within the same `state`; explicitly notes `importance`/`freshness` are not discussed and lifecycle `state` is unaffected by type/confidence. **ADR 0014** (stance/register): added `stance` "formal|casual", excluded from `wakil query`'s default grounding context (not from `wakil search`). Both are Memory-row-level signals, not note-level.

**Key gap for a compression mechanism**: nothing in this schema tracks per-section "staleness"/"importance" of an entity *note's* Compiled Truth/Timeline content — `Memory.importance`/`freshness` exist as unused columns but apply to extracted memory rows, not to entity-note prose. **The closest existing precedent for "what to leave alone vs. what to touch" is `EntityResolution.relevance` (`central|notable|minor|peripheral`, from ADR 0015/`entity-resolve/SKILL.md`)** — a per-*enrichment-run* judgment about how much a source concerns an entity, already used to gate the revision call, not a persisted note-level signal. A compression mechanism would need a new mechanism (either a new Memory/Note column, or purely content-derived heuristics like Timeline entry age/count) since nothing currently exists to rank *entity note* content by importance/age at rest.

### 4. CLI patterns for standalone/maintenance commands

Best close analog is **`wakil sources backfill-abstract`** (`sources_backfill_abstract`, `main.py:733-775`, backed by `plan_abstract_backfill`/`apply_abstract_backfill`, `ingest_service.py:401-463`): scans *every* Source in the workspace (not scoped to one source id), one capture-metadata model call per stale item, prints a plan, single yes/no confirm, then applies — rewriting each raw file's frontmatter via a byte-preserving `python-frontmatter` round-trip. **Notably, this command does not call `git_service.prepare_landing`/`land_ingestion` at all** — it writes directly to the working tree with no branch/commit, diverging from ADR 0003's git-native principle. This is a real precedent to note but not necessarily a template to copy for entity compression, given ADR 0003/CLAUDE.md's explicit instruction to show reviewable diffs for knowledge-base modifications.

The better-fitting analog, including a real diff preview, is **`wakil schema migrate`** (`schema_migrate`, `main.py:897-970`, backed by `plan_schema_migration`/`apply_migrations`, `src/wakil/app/schema_migrate_service.py`): scans all indexed notes (optionally filtered by `--type`), builds `MigrationProposal`s with unified diffs, supports `--dry-run` (print diffs, write nothing), a per-type "Apply N fix(es)? [y/N/d=show diffs]" prompt (`d` re-shows the diff on demand), `apply_migrations` re-reads each file immediately before writing and reports (not silently drops) stale files changed since planning, and an optional `--commit` that calls `git_service.commit_change(config, written, "chore", description)` — a **plain local commit, not the per-source branch/PR lifecycle**, explicitly documented as such in `git_service.py`'s module docstring. This is the closest existing shape for a periodic, whole-workspace "compress entities" command: plan (read-only, model calls) → per-batch diff preview → confirm → apply (re-read-and-guard) → optional `wakil chore:`-style commit, independent of any single `Source`/branch.

Module docstring at `ingest_service.py:1-27` names the two-phase discipline explicitly: "Each step is itself two-phase (prepare → preview/confirm → apply): prepare touches nothing, files are only ever created (never overwritten), and DB rows are only written in apply, so declining a preview leaves no trace."

### 5. Git-native change tracking / reviewable diffs

`docs/adr/0003-git-native-change-tracking.md`: decision to land all wakil-driven KB changes via git branches/commits/(optional) PRs rather than direct working-tree writes, "satisfying the working agreement's 'show reviewable diffs for knowledge-base modifications' and 'do not silently rewrite user knowledge.'" Two live mechanisms exist in `src/wakil/app/git_service.py`:

- **Per-source branch/PR lifecycle** (`prepare_landing`/`land_ingestion`/`abandon_landing`, lines 132-225): one branch + one PR tracked per `Source` row (`Source.git_branch`/`git_pr_url`) across capture→enrich; draft after capture, flipped ready on enrichment; staging is scoped to exactly the files wakil wrote (`git.stage_and_commit(root, files, message)`), never `git add -A`; `ensure_clean_for_branch` refuses to start on top of uncommitted user changes.
- **Plain local commit** (`commit_change`, lines 111-129): used by `schema migrate --commit`, no branch/PR — "a plain local commit, not part of the per-source branch/PR lifecycle."

A periodic "compress entities" mechanism, since it isn't tied to a single Source, would naturally either (a) use the `commit_change`/`chore` pattern (like `schema migrate --commit`) for a batch of touched entity notes, or (b) get its own dedicated branch (à la `ingest_branch_name`) if the team wants full PR review. Either way `commit_message(kind, description)` requires `kind` in `COMMIT_PREFIXES = ("ingest", "note", "link", "memory", "dream", "source", "chore")` — a new kind (e.g. `"compress"`) would need adding to that tuple/emoji map, or reuse `"chore"`.

### 6. Token/length budgeting code

`src/wakil/llm/client.py`:
- `DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS = 8192` (line 19).
- `ModelTruncatedError` (26-42): raised when `stop_reason/finish_reason == "max_tokens"/"length"`, carries `max_tokens` and the partial text.
- `AnthropicClient.complete` (66-102) hardcodes `thinking={"type": "adaptive"}` on every call — per ADR 0015, this consumes an unbounded, unpredictable share of `max_tokens` before any output text (one observed case: 96% of budget went to thinking, not output).

`src/wakil/llm/schemas.py`:
- `complete_with_contract` (177-220): one retry total; on `ModelTruncatedError` doubles `max_tokens` (8192→16384) and retries once more, then raises `ModelContractError(schema.__name__, str(exc), truncated=True)`; on `ValidationError`, appends the error to the prompt and retries once, then raises `truncated=False`. `ModelContractError.truncated` (schemas.py:24-32) is the structured flag downstream code branches on (used by `_revise_candidates`'s bisection).

`src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py` character-level budgets: `MAX_SOURCE_CHARS = 24_000` (source text truncation at extraction/resolution/revision), `GUIDE_MAX_CHARS = 4_000` (RESOLVER.md excerpt), `RELATED_NOTE_LIMIT = 5`. No existing budget on **existing-note content** sent into the revision prompt — `build_revision_prompt` inlines each target's *full* current file content (`llm/prompts.py:222-223`, `for path, content in targets: ...f"### Existing note to consider: {path}\n\n{content}"`), which is exactly the growth vector ADR 0015 diagnoses and exactly what a compression mechanism would need to bound.

`docs/adr/0015-relevance-gated-entities-and-truncation-driven-batching.md` is the directly relevant prior design work: it already diagnosed a real production truncation (`companies/mosaic-private-markets.md` ~53KB, `people/edward-bridges.md` ~32KB as cost drivers) and landed two mitigations — relevance filtering (Decision 1, implemented) and truncation-driven recursive bisection (Decision 2/Step B, implemented in the code read above). It explicitly frames both as *workarounds for an unbounded existing-note size*, not a fix to the size itself — this is the natural motivating precedent/rationale to cite for why an entity-compression mechanism is now needed as the next step; its "Alternatives Considered" and "Consequences" sections (worth reading in full for the plan) already note the batching mechanism "does not eliminate truncation risk outright: a single entity whose own existing note is large enough to overflow the budget by itself... is a real, surfaced failure."

### 7. Existing tests / realistic Compiled Truth / Timeline fixture markdown

`tests/unit/test_ingest_service.py` (grep hits at lines 528-1126) is the relevant file (`test_entity_resolution.py` only has 2 incidental hits, no real fixtures). Real fixture content, `REAL_SHAPED_PERSON` (lines 736-753) — deliberately "mirrors actual entity pages in production use, not an idealized one":
```markdown
---
type: person
name: Priya Shah
status: active
tags:
  - job-search
created: 2026-06-01
updated: 2026-06-01
---

# priya-shah

**Recruiter** at [[companies/acme|Acme]]. First screen 2026-06-01.

Cross-references: [[companies/acme|Acme]]

---

## Timeline / Log

### 2026-06-01 — recruiter screen
- Introductory call, discussed the VP Eng role.

- **2026-06-01** | Referenced in [some-meeting](meetings/2026/2026-06-01-screen.md)
```
Note: no explicit `## Compiled Truth` heading here — the top section is just prose after the H1 (a real, un-idealized shape the merge code must tolerate). A second fixture, `REAL_SHAPED_PERSON_WITH_COMPILED_TRUTH_HEADING` (lines 803-820), does have the explicit heading, modeling the real `companies/mosaic-private-markets.md`:
```markdown
# acme

## Compiled Truth

AI-native widgets. Long-established prior analysis that must survive
any update where the model doesn't resend it.

Cross-references: [[people/priya-shah|Priya Shah]]

---

## Timeline / Log

### 2026-06-01 — recruiter screen
- Introductory call.

- **2026-06-01** | Referenced in [some-meeting](meetings/2026/2026-06-01-screen.md)
```
Both fixtures include a trailing **auto-generated back-link bullet** (`- **2026-06-01** | Referenced in [...]`) after the dated Timeline entries — tests assert this survives untouched across merges (line 779). `_stub_content` (`ingest_service.py:1244-1255`) is the canonical fresh skeleton: `## Compiled Truth` / `_Synthesized current state — rewrite when facts change._` / `## Open Threads` / `---` / `## Timeline / Log`. The test suite also covers a **legacy shape** (`## Timeline` without `/ Log`, line 870) that the merge regex must still recognize (`_TIMELINE_HEADING_RE`, `ingest_service.py:1021`).

---

### Notes for the compression-mechanism plan

- The single largest architectural fact for this plan is that ADR 0015 has already identified and started solving the exact problem (unbounded entity-note size feeding into a single-source-scoped model call) with a *reactive/per-run* mechanism (relevance filtering + truncation bisection). Entity compression would be the natural *proactive, periodic, cross-source* complement — shrinking the notes themselves rather than working around their size at revision time.
- Any compression call must go through a dedicated skill (not `note-revision` or `entity-enrichment`, whose entire design treats shrinkage as a red flag/"clobbering bug") with an explicit mandate to compress older Timeline entries into Compiled Truth and/or truncate old Timeline detail, while still following the same prepare→diff-preview→confirm→apply, stale-file-guard, and git-landing discipline every other write path in this codebase uses.
- There is no existing per-note or per-entity "importance"/"age" signal in the DB (`Memory.importance`/`freshness` are unused columns scoped to extracted memories, not entity notes); a compression mechanism will likely need to derive staleness from the Timeline's own dated entries (parseable via the same `_TIMELINE_HEADING_RE`/dated-entry conventions already in `ingest_service.py`) rather than from any DB column, or introduce a new signal.
- `schema_migrate_service.py`'s plan/diff/apply/stale-guard/optional-`chore`-commit shape (not `sources backfill-abstract`'s no-git shape) is the better template to follow, both structurally and per ADR 0003/CLAUDE.md's reviewable-diff requirement.

And its named failure mode, "the clobbering bug":

> "Prefer surgical edits — append a Timeline entry, edit the State block — over rewriting an existing page wholesale. Treat 'my new version is shorter than the old one' as a stop-and-check signal, not something to wave through."

This is directly in tension with what a compression mechanism must do (deliberately shrink content) — any compression design needs an explicit, separate code path/skill that is allowed to shrink Compiled Truth/Timeline, since both `note-revision` and `entity-enrichment` treat shrinkage as a red flag by design.

### 3. Database schema for Memory / Relationship / Note / Source

`src/wakil/storage/schema.py`. Relevant `Memory` columns (lines 82-113):
```
memory_type: String(30)   # free-string: fact|opinion|summary|relationship|question|hypothesis|decision|theme|event
content: Text
confidence: float | None  # 0.0-1.0, identity/certainty-ish signal (ADR 0013)
stance: String(10) | None # "formal"|"casual" — commitment/register axis (ADR 0014); NOT "register" at ORM level (Pydantic ABCMeta collision)
state: String(20) = "working"   # actually always "candidate" at write time per apply_enrichment; promote/reject/archive move it
importance: float | None  # column exists but nothing in ingest_service.py writes it
freshness: float | None   # column exists but nothing in ingest_service.py writes it
event_date: date | None   # the described event's own date, for Timeline ordering
last_seen_at: datetime | None
created_at / updated_at
```
`Note` (67-79) has `path`, `title`, `frontmatter_json`, `content_hash`, `last_indexed_at` — no register/importance columns; entity pages' "importance" lives only in the markdown (frontmatter/content), not the DB. `Source`/`Relationship`/`IngestRun` as expected; no schema field distinguishes old vs. new content within a note.

**ADR 0013** (opinion type + confidence-as-ranking): confidence became a `search_memories`/`retrieval_rank` tiebreak only within the same `state`; explicitly notes `importance`/`freshness` are not discussed and lifecycle `state` is unaffected by type/confidence. **ADR 0014** (stance/register): added `stance` "formal|casual", excluded from `wakil query`'s default grounding context (not from `wakil search`). Both are Memory-row-level signals, not note-level.

**Key gap for a compression mechanism**: nothing in this schema tracks per-section "staleness"/"importance" of an entity *note's* Compiled Truth/Timeline content — `Memory.importance`/`freshness` exist as unused columns but apply to extracted memory rows, not to entity-note prose. **The closest existing precedent for "what to leave alone vs. what to touch" is `EntityResolution.relevance` (`central|notable|minor|peripheral`, from ADR 0015/`entity-resolve/SKILL.md`)** — a per-*enrichment-run* judgment about how much a source concerns an entity, already used to gate the revision call, not a persisted note-level signal. A compression mechanism would need a new mechanism (either a new Memory/Note column, or purely content-derived heuristics like Timeline entry age/count) since nothing currently exists to rank *entity note* content by importance/age at rest.

### 4. CLI patterns for standalone/maintenance commands

Best close analog is **`wakil sources backfill-abstract`** (`sources_backfill_abstract`, `main.py:733-775`, backed by `plan_abstract_backfill`/`apply_abstract_backfill`, `ingest_service.py:401-463`): scans *every* Source in the workspace (not scoped to one source id), one capture-metadata model call per stale item, prints a plan, single yes/no confirm, then applies — rewriting each raw file's frontmatter via a byte-preserving `python-frontmatter` round-trip. **Notably, this command does not call `git_service.prepare_landing`/`land_ingestion` at all** — it writes directly to the working tree with no branch/commit, diverging from ADR 0003's git-native principle. This is a real precedent to note but not necessarily a template to copy for entity compression, given ADR 0003/CLAUDE.md's explicit instruction to show reviewable diffs for knowledge-base modifications.

The better-fitting analog, including a real diff preview, is **`wakil schema migrate`** (`schema_migrate`, `main.py:897-970`, backed by `plan_schema_migration`/`apply_migrations`, `src/wakil/app/schema_migrate_service.py`): scans all indexed notes (optionally filtered by `--type`), builds `MigrationProposal`s with unified diffs, supports `--dry-run` (print diffs, write nothing), a per-type "Apply N fix(es)? [y/N/d=show diffs]" prompt (`d` re-shows the diff on demand), `apply_migrations` re-reads each file immediately before writing and reports (not silently drops) stale files changed since planning, and an optional `--commit` that calls `git_service.commit_change(config, written, "chore", description)` — a **plain local commit, not the per-source branch/PR lifecycle**, explicitly documented as such in `git_service.py`'s module docstring. This is the closest existing shape for a periodic, whole-workspace "compress entities" command: plan (read-only, model calls) → per-batch diff preview → confirm → apply (re-read-and-guard) → optional `wakil chore:`-style commit, independent of any single `Source`/branch.

Module docstring at `ingest_service.py:1-27` names the two-phase discipline explicitly: "Each step is itself two-phase (prepare → preview/confirm → apply): prepare touches nothing, files are only ever created (never overwritten), and DB rows are only written in apply, so declining a preview leaves no trace."

### 5. Git-native change tracking / reviewable diffs

`docs/adr/0003-git-native-change-tracking.md`: decision to land all wakil-driven KB changes via git branches/commits/(optional) PRs rather than direct working-tree writes, "satisfying the working agreement's 'show reviewable diffs for knowledge-base modifications' and 'do not silently rewrite user knowledge.'" Two live mechanisms exist in `src/wakil/app/git_service.py`:

- **Per-source branch/PR lifecycle** (`prepare_landing`/`land_ingestion`/`abandon_landing`, lines 132-225): one branch + one PR tracked per `Source` row (`Source.git_branch`/`git_pr_url`) across capture→enrich; draft after capture, flipped ready on enrichment; staging is scoped to exactly the files wakil wrote (`git.stage_and_commit(root, files, message)`), never `git add -A`; `ensure_clean_for_branch` refuses to start on top of uncommitted user changes.
- **Plain local commit** (`commit_change`, lines 111-129): used by `schema migrate --commit`, no branch/PR — "a plain local commit, not part of the per-source branch/PR lifecycle."

A periodic "compress entities" mechanism, since it isn't tied to a single Source, would naturally either (a) use the `commit_change`/`chore` pattern (like `schema migrate --commit`) for a batch of touched entity notes, or (b) get its own dedicated branch (à la `ingest_branch_name`) if the team wants full PR review. Either way `commit_message(kind, description)` requires `kind` in `COMMIT_PREFIXES = ("ingest", "note", "link", "memory", "dream", "source", "chore")` — a new kind (e.g. `"compress"`) would need adding to that tuple/emoji map, or reuse `"chore"`.

### 6. Token/length budgeting code

`src/wakil/llm/client.py`:
- `DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS = 8192` (line 19).
- `ModelTruncatedError` (26-42): raised when `stop_reason/finish_reason == "max_tokens"/"length"`, carries `max_tokens` and the partial text.
- `AnthropicClient.complete` (66-102) hardcodes `thinking={"type": "adaptive"}` on every call — per ADR 0015, this consumes an unbounded, unpredictable share of `max_tokens` before any output text (one observed case: 96% of budget went to thinking, not output).

`src/wakil/llm/schemas.py`:
- `complete_with_contract` (177-220): one retry total; on `ModelTruncatedError` doubles `max_tokens` (8192→16384) and retries once more, then raises `ModelContractError(schema.__name__, str(exc), truncated=True)`; on `ValidationError`, appends the error to the prompt and retries once, then raises `truncated=False`. `ModelContractError.truncated` (schemas.py:24-32) is the structured flag downstream code branches on (used by `_revise_candidates`'s bisection).

`src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py` character-level budgets: `MAX_SOURCE_CHARS = 24_000` (source text truncation at extraction/resolution/revision), `GUIDE_MAX_CHARS = 4_000` (RESOLVER.md excerpt), `RELATED_NOTE_LIMIT = 5`. No existing budget on **existing-note content** sent into the revision prompt — `build_revision_prompt` inlines each target's *full* current file content (`llm/prompts.py:222-223`, `for path, content in targets: ...f"### Existing note to consider: {path}\n\n{content}"`), which is exactly the growth vector ADR 0015 diagnoses and exactly what a compression mechanism would need to bound.

`docs/adr/0015-relevance-gated-entities-and-truncation-driven-batching.md` is the directly relevant prior design work: it already diagnosed a real production truncation (`companies/mosaic-private-markets.md` ~53KB, `people/edward-bridges.md` ~32KB as cost drivers) and landed two mitigations — relevance filtering (Decision 1, implemented) and truncation-driven recursive bisection (Decision 2/Step B, implemented in the code read above). It explicitly frames both as *workarounds for an unbounded existing-note size*, not a fix to the size itself — this is the natural motivating precedent/rationale to cite for why an entity-compression mechanism is now needed as the next step; its "Alternatives Considered" and "Consequences" sections (worth reading in full for the plan) already note the batching mechanism "does not eliminate truncation risk outright: a single entity whose own existing note is large enough to overflow the budget by itself... is a real, surfaced failure."

### 7. Existing tests / realistic Compiled Truth / Timeline fixture markdown

`tests/unit/test_ingest_service.py` (grep hits at lines 528-1126) is the relevant file (`test_entity_resolution.py` only has 2 incidental hits, no real fixtures). Real fixture content, `REAL_SHAPED_PERSON` (lines 736-753) — deliberately "mirrors actual entity pages in production use, not an idealized one":
```markdown
---
type: person
name: Priya Shah
status: active
tags:
  - job-search
created: 2026-06-01
updated: 2026-06-01
---

# priya-shah

**Recruiter** at [[companies/acme|Acme]]. First screen 2026-06-01.

Cross-references: [[companies/acme|Acme]]

---

## Timeline / Log

### 2026-06-01 — recruiter screen
- Introductory call, discussed the VP Eng role.

- **2026-06-01** | Referenced in [some-meeting](meetings/2026/2026-06-01-screen.md)
```
Note: no explicit `## Compiled Truth` heading here — the top section is just prose after the H1 (a real, un-idealized shape the merge code must tolerate). A second fixture, `REAL_SHAPED_PERSON_WITH_COMPILED_TRUTH_HEADING` (lines 803-820), does have the explicit heading, modeling the real `companies/mosaic-private-markets.md`:
```markdown
# acme

## Compiled Truth

AI-native widgets. Long-established prior analysis that must survive
any update where the model doesn't resend it.

Cross-references: [[people/priya-shah|Priya Shah]]

---

## Timeline / Log

### 2026-06-01 — recruiter screen
- Introductory call.

- **2026-06-01** | Referenced in [some-meeting](meetings/2026/2026-06-01-screen.md)
```
Both fixtures include a trailing **auto-generated back-link bullet** (`- **2026-06-01** | Referenced in [...]`) after the dated Timeline entries — tests assert this survives untouched across merges (line 779). `_stub_content` (`ingest_service.py:1244-1255`) is the canonical fresh skeleton: `## Compiled Truth` / `_Synthesized current state — rewrite when facts change._` / `## Open Threads` / `---` / `## Timeline / Log`. The test suite also covers a **legacy shape** (`## Timeline` without `/ Log`, line 870) that the merge regex must still recognize (`_TIMELINE_HEADING_RE`, `ingest_service.py:1021`).

---

### Notes for the compression-mechanism plan

- The single largest architectural fact for this plan is that ADR 0015 has already identified and started solving the exact problem (unbounded entity-note size feeding into a single-source-scoped model call) with a *reactive/per-run* mechanism (relevance filtering + truncation bisection). Entity compression would be the natural *proactive, periodic, cross-source* complement — shrinking the notes themselves rather than working around their size at revision time.
- Any compression call must go through a dedicated skill (not `note-revision` or `entity-enrichment`, whose entire design treats shrinkage as a red flag/"clobbering bug") with an explicit mandate to compress older Timeline entries into Compiled Truth and/or truncate old Timeline detail, while still following the same prepare→diff-preview→confirm→apply, stale-file-guard, and git-landing discipline every other write path in this codebase uses.
- There is no existing per-note or per-entity "importance"/"age" signal in the DB (`Memory.importance`/`freshness` are unused columns scoped to extracted memories, not entity notes); a compression mechanism will likely need to derive staleness from the Timeline's own dated entries (parseable via the same `_TIMELINE_HEADING_RE`/dated-entry conventions already in `ingest_service.py`) rather than from any DB column, or introduce a new signal.
- `schema_migrate_service.py`'s plan/diff/apply/stale-guard/optional-`chore`-commit shape (not `sources backfill-abstract`'s no-git shape) is the better template to follow, both structurally and per ADR 0003/CLAUDE.md's reviewable-diff requirement.
