---

# Research Report: Entity Compression Mechanism — Current State of Compiled Truth / Timeline

## 0. Important context discovered: uncommitted working-tree changes

Before the substance: `git status` shows **uncommitted modifications** to `src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`, `src/wakil/llm/schemas.py`, two test files, `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`, `docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md`, and the entire new file `docs/adr/0015-relevance-gated-entities-and-truncation-driven-batching.md` (372 new lines), relative to `HEAD` (`a656537`). Everything described below reflects the **working tree as it currently stands**, not just the last commit — this includes the full ADR 0015 batching/bisection mechanism (item 5 below), which the ADR's own prose describes as "not yet implemented" but which is in fact already coded in the working tree. Worth flagging to whoever plans the next commit.

---

## 1. Entity note markdown structure

**Canonical template**: `src/wakil/schema/templates/compiled-truth-timeline.md` (referenced by every entity schema via `page_shape: compiled-truth-timeline`):

```markdown
# {Display Name}

## Compiled Truth

{synthesized, always-current summary — cite non-obvious claims inline}
- {state fields relevant to this subject}

### Open threads
- {what's unresolved}

Cross-references: [[other-entity]]

---

## Timeline / Log

### {date} — source: {kind}
- {what happened / what was learned, cited}
```

Design doc: `docs/entity-model.md` (lines 88-125) — same shape, documents that `## Open Threads` should be its own H2 (not the inline bullet the target vault's `schema.md` originally specified), giving `wakil` "a stable H2→H2 parse boundary."

**Schema wiring** — `src/wakil/schema/entities/person.yaml` and `company.yaml` (and `concept.yaml`, `project.yaml` presumably similar): `page_shape: compiled-truth-timeline`, `category: identity`, `directory: people` / `companies`, with required `created`/`updated` date fields. `_run_entity_updates` (ingest_service.py:1108-1116) filters candidates to `schema.page_shape != "compiled-truth-timeline"` before running the revision call at all — only identity-type entities get this two-part treatment.

**Real-world shape is looser than the template** (per `docs/entity-model.md` §"What the pattern looks like in practice", and the `REAL_SHAPED_PERSON` fixtures in `tests/unit/test_ingest_service.py:731-751`):
- No explicit `## Compiled Truth` heading on many real pages — prose right after the H1 is treated as the "top section."
- `## Timeline` (no `/ Log` suffix) on 36 real notes, predating that convention (`docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md:150-154`).
- Some pages (`people/jane-doe.md`) have no Timeline heading at all — `_merge_entity_note` returns `None` for these; the caller surfaces a warning and leaves the note untouched.
- Auto-generated back-link bullets (`- **date** | Referenced in [...]`) live inside the Timeline section, at the very bottom, and must never be touched by any merge.

**Code that parses this shape** (`src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`):
- `_H1_RE = re.compile(r"(?m)^#\s+.*$")` (line 1016)
- `_TIMELINE_HEADING_RE = re.compile(r"(?m)^##\s+Timeline(?:\s*/\s*Log)?\s*$")` (line 1021)
- Everything between the H1 match and the Timeline-heading match is "the top section" (Compiled Truth, whether or not it has its own `## Compiled Truth` H2).

**Stub skeleton** written by `_stub_content` (ingest_service.py:1244-1255) for newly-created entities:
```
# {name}

## Compiled Truth

_Synthesized current state — rewrite when facts change._

## Open Threads

---

## Timeline / Log
```

---

## 2. How Timeline entries are created and formatted

- **No dedicated Timeline-entry data model in code today.** The design intent (`docs/adr/0005-timeline-entries-as-memory-rows.md`) is that a Timeline entry *should* eventually be a `Memory` row with `memory_type='event'`, `note_id` set to the entity, `source_id` set to the source, and a new `event_date` column (rejecting a dedicated `timeline_entries` table, reusing `Memory`'s existing lifecycle). **This is not implemented in `apply_enrichment`** — `Memory` rows are created (ingest_service.py:1384-1397) with `memory_type`, `content`, `confidence`, `stance`, `event_date` fields, but nothing currently links a `Memory` row to the literal text prepended into a note's Timeline section; the Timeline text and the `Memory` table are two independent write paths today.
- **What actually happens**: `EntityRevision.timeline_entry: str | None` (llm/schemas.py:153-158) — a single free-text string the model produces per revised entity, e.g. `"### 2026-07-16 — second search kicked off\n- New role, same recruiter."` — no structured date/confidence/source fields, just Markdown text the model is asked to format as `### {date} — {what happened}\n- {detail}`.
- **Insertion**: `_insert_timeline_entry` (ingest_service.py:1024-1035) prepends this text as the new first entry right after the `## Timeline / Log` heading line, before every existing entry (including trailing back-link bullets), which are never touched.
- **Merge**: `_merge_entity_note` (ingest_service.py:1041-1085) does a deterministic, surgical (never full-file) merge: parses frontmatter via `python-frontmatter`, finds H1 and Timeline-heading positions via the regexes above, replaces only the top section with `revision.compiled_truth` (falling back to old content if empty — see §3), and calls `_insert_timeline_entry` for the Timeline half. Frontmatter `updated` is always stamped to `today`.

**ADR 0005** ("Timeline Entries Live in Memory, Not a Dedicated `timeline_entries` Table") — accepted design intent, not yet wired up: reuse `Memory` table, one new nullable `Memory.event_date` column, reject a GBrain-style dedicated table to avoid forking the promotion/dedup lifecycle.

`docs/memory-model.md` frames this more broadly: durable Markdown content changes must always be a reviewable proposal/diff, never an autonomous background rewrite ("Where this meets wakil's principles" section, lines 202-210) — directly relevant to any compression mechanism, which would be exactly this kind of durable-content rewrite.

---

## 3. How "Compiled Truth" is created/merged today

- **Model-generated per enrichment run**, via `EntityRevision.compiled_truth` (llm/schemas.py:137-158): "For has_update=True: the full re-synthesized top section — the union of what was already there plus what's new, never just the new source's content." The model is instructed to re-derive the whole section from everything it's shown (old note content + new source), not diff/append.
- **Not purely appended** — it's a full replace of "the top section" (everything between H1 and Timeline heading), but the *input* to that replace is supposed to be the union of old + new (re-synthesis), enforced only by prompt instruction (`entity-enrichment/SKILL.md` "Texture over facts", `note-revision/SKILL.md` "State vs. Timeline"), not by any code-level guarantee that old facts survive.
- **The clobbering bug** (`docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md:168-177`, section header literally "`enrich` replaced an entire '## Compiled Truth' section with nothing (the clobbering bug, in wakil's own merge code)"): `has_update=True` legitimately can mean "only Timeline changed, Compiled Truth needs no re-synthesis" — but `_merge_entity_note` originally treated an empty/absent `compiled_truth` as "the top section is now empty" and wrote that, wiping a long carefully-synthesized section. **Fix, now in code** (line 1074-1080):
  ```python
  compiled_truth = (revision.compiled_truth or "").strip() or old_top
  new_top = f"{h1_line}\n\n{compiled_truth}\n\n---" if compiled_truth else h1_line
  ```
  i.e., empty `compiled_truth` from the model falls back to the *existing* top section verbatim, never to blank.
- There is **no separate `wakil entity compile <slug>` command yet** — `docs/entity-model.md` (§"Write / promotion path", item 4) proposes this as a future, dedicated synthesis command scoped only to Compiled Truth + Open Threads (never touching Timeline), producing a surgical diff of just that section, committed via `GitChange(operation="entity_compile")`. `docs/ingestion-refactor-spec.md:48` lists it explicitly as **deferred / out of scope** for the current refactor. This is the natural existing "hook" a compression mechanism could piggyback on or must be designed alongside.
- System prompt for this call comes from `src/wakil/skills/note-revision/SKILL.md` (loaded via `load_skill("note-revision", ...)` at ingest_service.py:1217) plus `EntityRevisionOutput`'s Pydantic schema. Key discipline: "Diff your draft against the current page before saving. If the new version is shorter, or drops a fact/frontmatter key that was there before, stop — you are very likely clobbering, not updating" (Step 5), and "Never replace a developed note with a freshly generated summary, even when the summary is accurate."

---

## 4. How entity note content is loaded into context when enriching a NEW source

**Confirmed: the entire file (Compiled Truth + Timeline, verbatim) is loaded and sent to the model** for every candidate that survives relevance gating.

- `_run_entity_updates` (ingest_service.py:1120-1135) reads the *whole file*: `content = target.read_text(encoding="utf-8")` and stores `(resolution, target_path, content)` tuples as `candidates`.
- `_revise_candidates` (ingest_service.py:1203-1241) passes `targets = [(res.target_note_path, content) for res, _, content in candidates]` straight into `build_revision_prompt`.
- `build_revision_prompt` (llm/prompts.py:175-226) inlines full content per target:
  ```python
  for path, content in targets:
      suffix_parts += [f"### Existing note to consider: {path}\n\n{content}", ""]
  ```
  Its own docstring is explicit about why: *"The system prompt is `note-revision/SKILL.md` itself — its 'read the existing note in full before writing anything' rule is why the full content is inlined here rather than a summary or a diff."*
- This is exactly the "cost driver" ADR 0015 diagnoses: it cites `companies/mosaic-private-markets.md` at **~53KB** and `people/edward-bridges.md` at **~32KB** of existing content contributing to a ~68K-input-token request that then still overflowed the 16384-token *output* budget (input size wasn't even the direct trigger — see §5).
- `_candidate_entity_notes` (ingest_service.py:772-816) is the direct title-lookup step that supplies candidate `related_notes` for the *first two* DAG calls (extraction, resolution) — it never reads file content, only `Note.title`, matching proper-noun phrases against note titles. It does **not** feed the revision call directly (revision candidates come from `entity_resolutions` with `action="update"`, resolved earlier).
- Separately, `prepare_enrichment` also builds `related_notes` (search-hit list, title + short snippet only, not full content) that feeds the extraction and resolution prompts via `_render_related` (llm/prompts.py:281-284) — that path is cheap (titles only) and is **not** where the cost lives; the expensive full-file inlining is specific to the revision call (`build_revision_prompt`).

**Conclusion relevant to the user's actual request**: today there is no distinction at all between Compiled Truth and Timeline when building revision-call context — the code doesn't even parse them apart before sending; it sends the raw file bytes. Splitting so only Compiled Truth is sent would require either (a) parsing out the top section using the same `_H1_RE`/`_TIMELINE_HEADING_RE` logic `_merge_entity_note` already has, and sending only that, or (b) something that pre-compresses Timeline into the Compiled Truth text so nothing is lost by omitting Timeline. Note the load-bearing tension: `note-revision/SKILL.md`'s "read the existing note in full" instruction and the re-synthesis discipline ("union of what was already known plus new") were written assuming full-file visibility — the model currently uses Timeline content as part of what it's re-synthesizing from. If Timeline is dropped from context, any fact that lives *only* in Timeline (not yet promoted into Compiled Truth) becomes invisible to future re-synthesis, silently regressing exactly the kind of fact the project's "never silently rewrite/lose user knowledge" principle is meant to protect — this is a real design question, not just an implementation detail, and should be central to the plan.

---

## 5. `ModelTruncatedError` / `ModelContractError.truncated` and `_split_candidates_by_content_length`

**`ModelTruncatedError`** — `src/wakil/llm/client.py:26-42`:
```python
class ModelTruncatedError(ModelError):
    """The provider stopped generating because it hit max_tokens.
    ... callers can retry with a larger budget instead of re-prompting for the same length."""
    def __init__(self, max_tokens: int, partial: str):
```
Raised by both `AnthropicClient.complete` (line 101) and `OpenAICompatibleClient.complete` (line 150) when the provider reports `stop_reason == "max_tokens"` / `finish_reason == "length"` (per `docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md`'s entry, dated 2026-07-20).

**Handling** — `complete_with_contract` (`src/wakil/llm/schemas.py:177-220`): one retry loop, `max_tokens = DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS` (8192) initially:
- `ModelTruncatedError` on attempt 1 → **doubles `max_tokens`**, resends identical prompt (truncation isn't a content problem, resending unchanged just truncates again at the same length).
- `ModelTruncatedError` on attempt 2 → raises `ModelContractError(schema.__name__, str(exc), truncated=True)`.
- `ValidationError` (malformed but not truncated) → attempt 1 appends the validation error to the prompt and retries; attempt 2 raises `ModelContractError(..., truncated=False)`.
- `ModelContractError.truncated: bool` (schemas.py:21-33) is the structured flag callers branch on — added specifically so `_revise_candidates` can distinguish "split and retry" from "this will fail identically on a smaller batch too."

**`_split_candidates_by_content_length`** (`ingest_service.py:1151-1171`) — greedy 2-way balance by **existing-note content length** (not entity count): sorts candidates longest-first, then places each into whichever running half currently has less accumulated content length, isolating the single biggest note from compounding with the next-biggest. Called from `_revise_candidates` (line 1228) only when `exc.truncated and len(candidates) > 1 and depth < _MAX_BISECTION_DEPTH` (`_MAX_BISECTION_DEPTH = 3`, line 1095, "caps worst-case fan-out ... to at most 2**3 = 8 sub-batches"). This is **reactive**: it only fires after a real truncation has already happened, discovering the safe batch size empirically per-run rather than precomputing one.

**ADR 0015** (`docs/adr/0015-relevance-gated-entities-and-truncation-driven-batching.md`) is the design document for exactly this mechanism, and is essential reading for the compression plan — summary:
- **Decision 1 (relevance gating, implemented)**: `EntityResolution.relevance: central|notable|minor|peripheral`, judged free during resolution; `_run_entity_updates` excludes `minor`/`peripheral` before the expensive revision call (`_LOW_RELEVANCE = {"minor", "peripheral"}`, line 1091), surfaced as a `proposal.warnings` entry, never silent.
- **Decision 2 (batching, Step A tried/rejected, Step B implemented in the uncommitted working tree — §0 above)**: Step A tested `output_config={"effort": "low"}` and `thinking: {type: "disabled"}` live against the Anthropic API to bound *thinking*-token cost (the actual dominant cost driver — 96% of consumed budget in the original failure was reasoning tokens, not output text) — neither worked (`effort` barely moved the needle; `disabled` broke JSON compliance outright). Step B (the bisection above) is therefore "the operative mechanism for whatever truncation risk remains after relevance filtering," confirmed necessary by a live re-run where even the 4 `central`-relevance survivors (including `people/edward-bridges.md` at ~32KB) still truncated.
- Explicitly frames this as reactive: "a size discovered empirically from an actual truncation is more defensible than one guessed at design time" — and explicitly rejects a fixed batch-size-by-count as a primary mechanism, and rejects clustering-by-topic (an extra model call) since every candidate already shares the same cached source-document prefix.
- Names the compounding cost driver a proactive compression mechanism would directly attack: **`companies/mosaic-private-markets.md` at ~53KB was, on its own, larger than the other nine targets combined** in the original failing case.

This is exactly the "reactive mitigation" you asked me to characterize precisely: it only kicks in after the fact (post-truncation), operates per-run (not persisted anywhere), and its unit of batching is the *candidate set for one revision call*, not the *stored size of an entity note*. A proactive "periodically compress entities" mechanism would complement it by keeping the notes themselves smaller so both the per-call context and the batching math stay cheap in the first place — it wouldn't replace Step B's role as a last-resort safety valve when a single note is still too large to send even alone (the ADR explicitly leaves that failure mode as "a real, surfaced failure ... not silently papered over").

---

## 6. Existing "compression"/summarization-adjacent code

**None found.** Grepped `compress|summariz|prune` and `truncat` across `src/wakil/**/*.py`:
- `_summarize_source` (ingest_service.py:497) — unrelated; builds a `SourceSummary` display object (id/title/status) for `wakil sources` CLI listing, not content summarization.
- `prune=...` occurrences (workspace_service.py, ingest_service.py, schema_migrate_service.py) — all about `index_notes(..., prune=...)`, removing stale SQLite index rows for notes deleted from disk, unrelated to entity-content pruning.
- `decompressed` (ingest_service.py:700, a comment) — about unzipping the vendored common-words wordlist, unrelated.
- All `truncat*` hits are exactly the `ModelTruncatedError`/`ModelContractError.truncated` machinery already covered in §5 — nothing else.
- `docs/entity-model.md`'s proposed `wakil entity compile <slug>` command (§3 above) is the closest existing *design* to a compression mechanism, but it's explicitly deferred/unimplemented and its own scope (re-synthesize Compiled Truth + Open Threads from all durable Memory rows) is about *promoting* raw content into synthesized state, not about *shrinking* an already-large Compiled Truth or Timeline for context-budget reasons — a genuinely new concern your planned mechanism would need to define from scratch.

**Conclusion**: there is no scaffolding, no half-built attempt, no stub function or TODO anywhere in `src/wakil/` for entity-note compression/summarization. This is greenfield.

---

## 7. Relevant ADRs (full list, `docs/adr/`)

| ADR | Status | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| 0001 skill-resolution-precedence-first-match-wins | — | Not directly relevant (skill file precedence rules), skipped in depth. |
| 0002 qmd-first-class-search | — | Search engine choice; not directly relevant. |
| 0003 git-native-change-tracking | — | Commits as the change-tracking mechanism; relevant only insofar as any compression write should follow the same git-commit-per-operation pattern other durable writes use. |
| 0004 exclude-live-model-skill-evals-from-default-ci | — | Establishes the norm that new *judgment* guidance (as opposed to deterministic code) needs a live-model eval, not just unit tests — cited repeatedly by ADR 0015 and directly relevant: any new "should this entity be compressed now" judgment would need the same eval treatment. |
| **0005 timeline-entries-as-memory-rows** | Accepted, partially implemented | Timeline entries should be `Memory` rows (`memory_type='event'`, new `event_date` column), reusing the existing lifecycle rather than a dedicated `timeline_entries` table — but this reuse isn't actually wired into `apply_enrichment` yet (see §2). Directly relevant: any compression scheme that wants to reconstruct/verify Timeline content programmatically will currently have to parse Markdown text, not query structured rows. |
| 0006 backlinks-as-live-query-over-widened-relationship-table | Accepted | Backlinks (the "Referenced in [...]" bullets baked into Timeline text today) should become a live SQL query over a widened `Relationship` table instead of stored prose — relevant because any Timeline-preserving compression must not corrupt/lose these auto-generated bullet lines, which `note-revision`/`entity-enrichment` both call out as "never touched." |
| 0007 markdown-source-of-truth-sqlite-operational-store | Accepted | Compiled Truth content is Markdown-only, never stored in SQLite — git provides version/diff/revert history, deliberately avoiding a GBrain-style `page_versions` snapshot table. Directly relevant: a compression mechanism's "before" state is recoverable via `git log`/`git diff` on the note file itself, not a database table — any design should lean on that rather than inventing a new snapshot mechanism. |
| 0008 ingestion-decomposition-reject-multi-agent-mechanism | Accepted | Establishes the fixed classify/extract/resolve/enforce/finalize DAG (implemented as `prepare_capture`/`prepare_enrichment`/`apply_*` code, not agent-decided delegation) as the shape all ingestion work must fit, explicitly rejecting multi-agent orchestration per CLAUDE.md's design biases. A compression mechanism should likely be its own explicit DAG node or standalone command, not a new autonomous agent. |
| 0009 prioritize-context-referenced-notes-in-related-search | Accepted | `@file:`-referenced notes get privileged, non-relevance-gated inclusion in `related_notes`. Tangential; not directly about compression. |
| 0010 capture-time-title-and-abstract-generation | Accepted | One cheap model call at capture time generates title/abstract. Tangential — shows precedent for a cheap, separate, single-purpose model call outside the main enrich DAG (a compression command could follow this shape). |
| 0011 retire-schema-md-dependency / 0012 resolver-md-migration-strategy | Accepted | Migration away from the target-vault's own `SCHEMA.md`/`resolver.md` files toward wakil's own schema catalog (`src/wakil/schema/entities/*.yaml`). 0012 explicitly references entity-model.md's Compiled Truth/Timeline convention as one of the things being migrated onto wakil's own schema authority (line 124). Relevant as background on where the canonical page-shape definition now lives (in-repo YAML/templates, not the user's vault). |
| **0013 opinion-memory-type-and-confidence-ranking** | Accepted | Adds `memory_type='opinion'` as a free-string addition and repositions `confidence` as (also) a retrieval-ranking input, distinguishing observed fact from subjective interpretation. Not directly about compression, but establishes the `Memory` extension pattern (free-string type + new field) later reused by relevance (`EntityResolution.relevance`, ADR 0015) — a plausible template for whatever "should this entity be compressed" signal gets added. |
| **0014 memory-register-field-and-query-exclusion** | Accepted | Adds explicit `register: formal\|casual` field to `Memory`, excluded from query grounding by default (low-commitment "hot takes" shouldn't ground answers with full weight). Not directly about compression; same "new Memory field, new default-exclusion rule" pattern as 0013. |
| **0015 relevance-gated-entities-and-truncation-driven-batching** | Accepted, Decision 1 implemented + live-eval-gated as incomplete, Decision 2 implemented in the working tree (uncommitted) | Covered in full in §5. The single most load-bearing ADR for this project: names the exact failure mode (large existing notes → truncated revision responses), the reactive fix (relevance gating + truncation-triggered bisection batching), and explicitly notes the biggest cost driver observed (~53KB note) as evidence a proactive size-reduction approach would help. Also documents that lowering `thinking` effort/disabling thinking does **not** fix the underlying cost — meaning a compression mechanism that shrinks note *size* is one of the few levers actually confirmed to reduce request cost, as opposed to token-budget tuning which was tried and failed. |

I also grepped `docs/adr/*.md` for "compiled truth" and "context" directly — no ADR beyond 0015 (which discusses "the page's entire 'Compiled Truth' section, not just a diff" as the thing the revision call re-synthesizes) and 0007 (Compiled Truth storage location) mentions either term meaningfully; 0009's "context" hits are about `--context`/`@file:` CLI flags, unrelated to model context-window budget.

---

## 8. CLAUDE.md principles and any overriding per-directory guidance

**No nested `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md` files exist anywhere else in the repo** (`find` for both names, excluding `.venv`, returned only the root `/Users/ebridges/Projects/wakil/CLAUDE.md`) — nothing under `schema/` or `skills/` overrides or supplements it.

Principles from the root `CLAUDE.md` most load-bearing for a compression mechanism:

- **Design Biases → Prefer**: "clear memory lifecycle," "human review," "explicit commands," "small composable services."
- **Design Biases → Avoid**: "large agent frameworks," "hidden background behavior," "automatic rewriting without review," "multi-agent orchestration," "opaque memory systems."
- **Working Agreement for Agents**, items 9, 11, 12 are the most directly binding: *"Respect the distinction between raw sources, durable notes, and memory."* / *"Show reviewable diffs for knowledge-base modifications."* / *"Do not silently rewrite user knowledge."*
- **Prime Directive**: "Does this clearly improve local Markdown knowledge work for one user?" — gate for whether compression is worth building at all vs. e.g. just fixing the context-inclusion split.

These are echoed and reinforced everywhere in the skill/ADR layer already surveyed: `note-revision/SKILL.md`'s entire "clobbering bug" section, `docs/memory-model.md`'s "Where this meets wakil's principles" (explicitly: "Silent reconsolidation is exactly the thing wakil exists not to do... Anything that changes durable Markdown is a proposal surfaced for review, expressed as a diff, gated on confirmation"), and ADR 0015's own citation of CLAUDE.md items 11/12 as justification for surfacing relevance-exclusions as visible warnings rather than dropping them silently. Any entity-compression design should therefore almost certainly be: (a) an explicit, separately-invoked operation (not something that runs automatically inside `wakil enrich`), (b) diff-previewed and confirm-gated exactly like every other note write path (`apply_enrichment`'s stale-file re-read guard at ingest_service.py:1358-1375 is the concrete precedent to mirror), and (c) never destructive of raw evidence — git history (per ADR 0007) is treated as the durable safety net for "what did this note used to say," so compression can lean on `git log`/diff rather than needing its own undo mechanism, but the compressed *file* itself must not silently drop facts that live only in Timeline, per the tension flagged in §4.

This hook reminder relates to committing changes, which is not part of this read-only research task — no commit is being made, so nothing to act on there. I now have sufficient material to compile the full report.

---

# Research Report: Entity Compression Mechanism — Current State of Compiled Truth / Timeline

## 0. Important context discovered: uncommitted working-tree changes

Before the substance: `git status` shows **uncommitted modifications** to `src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`, `src/wakil/llm/schemas.py`, two test files, `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`, `docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md`, and the entire new file `docs/adr/0015-relevance-gated-entities-and-truncation-driven-batching.md` (372 new lines), relative to `HEAD` (`a656537`). Everything described below reflects the **working tree as it currently stands**, not just the last commit — this includes the full ADR 0015 batching/bisection mechanism (item 5 below), which the ADR's own prose describes as "not yet implemented" but which is in fact already coded in the working tree. Worth flagging to whoever plans the next commit.

---

## 1. Entity note markdown structure

**Canonical template**: `src/wakil/schema/templates/compiled-truth-timeline.md` (referenced by every entity schema via `page_shape: compiled-truth-timeline`):

```markdown
# {Display Name}

## Compiled Truth

{synthesized, always-current summary — cite non-obvious claims inline}
- {state fields relevant to this subject}

### Open threads
- {what's unresolved}

Cross-references: [[other-entity]]

---

## Timeline / Log

### {date} — source: {kind}
- {what happened / what was learned, cited}
```

Design doc: `docs/entity-model.md` (lines 88-125) — same shape, documents that `## Open Threads` should be its own H2 (not the inline bullet the target vault's `schema.md` originally specified), giving `wakil` "a stable H2→H2 parse boundary."

**Schema wiring** — `src/wakil/schema/entities/person.yaml` and `company.yaml` (and `concept.yaml`, `project.yaml` presumably similar): `page_shape: compiled-truth-timeline`, `category: identity`, `directory: people` / `companies`, with required `created`/`updated` date fields. `_run_entity_updates` (ingest_service.py:1108-1116) filters candidates to `schema.page_shape != "compiled-truth-timeline"` before running the revision call at all — only identity-type entities get this two-part treatment.

**Real-world shape is looser than the template** (per `docs/entity-model.md` §"What the pattern looks like in practice", and the `REAL_SHAPED_PERSON` fixtures in `tests/unit/test_ingest_service.py:731-751`):
- No explicit `## Compiled Truth` heading on many real pages — prose right after the H1 is treated as the "top section."
- `## Timeline` (no `/ Log` suffix) on 36 real notes, predating that convention (`docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md:150-154`).
- Some pages (`people/jane-doe.md`) have no Timeline heading at all — `_merge_entity_note` returns `None` for these; the caller surfaces a warning and leaves the note untouched.
- Auto-generated back-link bullets (`- **date** | Referenced in [...]`) live inside the Timeline section, at the very bottom, and must never be touched by any merge.

**Code that parses this shape** (`src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`):
- `_H1_RE = re.compile(r"(?m)^#\s+.*$")` (line 1016)
- `_TIMELINE_HEADING_RE = re.compile(r"(?m)^##\s+Timeline(?:\s*/\s*Log)?\s*$")` (line 1021)
- Everything between the H1 match and the Timeline-heading match is "the top section" (Compiled Truth, whether or not it has its own `## Compiled Truth` H2).

**Stub skeleton** written by `_stub_content` (ingest_service.py:1244-1255) for newly-created entities:
```
# {name}

## Compiled Truth

_Synthesized current state — rewrite when facts change._

## Open Threads

---

## Timeline / Log
```

---

## 2. How Timeline entries are created and formatted

- **No dedicated Timeline-entry data model in code today.** The design intent (`docs/adr/0005-timeline-entries-as-memory-rows.md`) is that a Timeline entry *should* eventually be a `Memory` row with `memory_type='event'`, `note_id` set to the entity, `source_id` set to the source, and a new `event_date` column (rejecting a dedicated `timeline_entries` table, reusing `Memory`'s existing lifecycle). **This is not implemented in `apply_enrichment`** — `Memory` rows are created (ingest_service.py:1384-1397) with `memory_type`, `content`, `confidence`, `stance`, `event_date` fields, but nothing currently links a `Memory` row to the literal text prepended into a note's Timeline section; the Timeline text and the `Memory` table are two independent write paths today.
- **What actually happens**: `EntityRevision.timeline_entry: str | None` (llm/schemas.py:153-158) — a single free-text string the model produces per revised entity, e.g. `"### 2026-07-16 — second search kicked off\n- New role, same recruiter."` — no structured date/confidence/source fields, just Markdown text the model is asked to format as `### {date} — {what happened}\n- {detail}`.
- **Insertion**: `_insert_timeline_entry` (ingest_service.py:1024-1035) prepends this text as the new first entry right after the `## Timeline / Log` heading line, before every existing entry (including trailing back-link bullets), which are never touched.
- **Merge**: `_merge_entity_note` (ingest_service.py:1041-1085) does a deterministic, surgical (never full-file) merge: parses frontmatter via `python-frontmatter`, finds H1 and Timeline-heading positions via the regexes above, replaces only the top section with `revision.compiled_truth` (falling back to old content if empty — see §3), and calls `_insert_timeline_entry` for the Timeline half. Frontmatter `updated` is always stamped to `today`.

**ADR 0005** ("Timeline Entries Live in Memory, Not a Dedicated `timeline_entries` Table") — accepted design intent, not yet wired up: reuse `Memory` table, one new nullable `Memory.event_date` column, reject a GBrain-style dedicated table to avoid forking the promotion/dedup lifecycle.

`docs/memory-model.md` frames this more broadly: durable Markdown content changes must always be a reviewable proposal/diff, never an autonomous background rewrite ("Where this meets wakil's principles" section, lines 202-210) — directly relevant to any compression mechanism, which would be exactly this kind of durable-content rewrite.

---

## 3. How "Compiled Truth" is created/merged today

- **Model-generated per enrichment run**, via `EntityRevision.compiled_truth` (llm/schemas.py:137-158): "For has_update=True: the full re-synthesized top section — the union of what was already there plus what's new, never just the new source's content." The model is instructed to re-derive the whole section from everything it's shown (old note content + new source), not diff/append.
- **Not purely appended** — it's a full replace of "the top section" (everything between H1 and Timeline heading), but the *input* to that replace is supposed to be the union of old + new (re-synthesis), enforced only by prompt instruction (`entity-enrichment/SKILL.md` "Texture over facts", `note-revision/SKILL.md` "State vs. Timeline"), not by any code-level guarantee that old facts survive.
- **The clobbering bug** (`docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md:168-177`, section header literally "`enrich` replaced an entire '## Compiled Truth' section with nothing (the clobbering bug, in wakil's own merge code)"): `has_update=True` legitimately can mean "only Timeline changed, Compiled Truth needs no re-synthesis" — but `_merge_entity_note` originally treated an empty/absent `compiled_truth` as "the top section is now empty" and wrote that, wiping a long carefully-synthesized section. **Fix, now in code** (line 1074-1080):
  ```python
  compiled_truth = (revision.compiled_truth or "").strip() or old_top
  new_top = f"{h1_line}\n\n{compiled_truth}\n\n---" if compiled_truth else h1_line
  ```
  i.e., empty `compiled_truth` from the model falls back to the *existing* top section verbatim, never to blank.
- There is **no separate `wakil entity compile <slug>` command yet** — `docs/entity-model.md` (§"Write / promotion path", item 4) proposes this as a future, dedicated synthesis command scoped only to Compiled Truth + Open Threads (never touching Timeline), producing a surgical diff of just that section, committed via `GitChange(operation="entity_compile")`. `docs/ingestion-refactor-spec.md:48` lists it explicitly as **deferred / out of scope** for the current refactor. This is the natural existing "hook" a compression mechanism could piggyback on or must be designed alongside.
- System prompt for this call comes from `src/wakil/skills/note-revision/SKILL.md` (loaded via `load_skill("note-revision", ...)` at ingest_service.py:1217) plus `EntityRevisionOutput`'s Pydantic schema. Key discipline: "Diff your draft against the current page before saving. If the new version is shorter, or drops a fact/frontmatter key that was there before, stop — you are very likely clobbering, not updating" (Step 5), and "Never replace a developed note with a freshly generated summary, even when the summary is accurate."

---

## 4. How entity note content is loaded into context when enriching a NEW source

**Confirmed: the entire file (Compiled Truth + Timeline, verbatim) is loaded and sent to the model** for every candidate that survives relevance gating.

- `_run_entity_updates` (ingest_service.py:1120-1135) reads the *whole file*: `content = target.read_text(encoding="utf-8")` and stores `(resolution, target_path, content)` tuples as `candidates`.
- `_revise_candidates` (ingest_service.py:1203-1241) passes `targets = [(res.target_note_path, content) for res, _, content in candidates]` straight into `build_revision_prompt`.
- `build_revision_prompt` (llm/prompts.py:175-226) inlines full content per target:
  ```python
  for path, content in targets:
      suffix_parts += [f"### Existing note to consider: {path}\n\n{content}", ""]
  ```
  Its own docstring is explicit about why: *"The system prompt is `note-revision/SKILL.md` itself — its 'read the existing note in full before writing anything' rule is why the full content is inlined here rather than a summary or a diff."*
- This is exactly the "cost driver" ADR 0015 diagnoses: it cites `companies/mosaic-private-markets.md` at **~53KB** and `people/edward-bridges.md` at **~32KB** of existing content contributing to a ~68K-input-token request that then still overflowed the 16384-token *output* budget (input size wasn't even the direct trigger — see §5).
- `_candidate_entity_notes` (ingest_service.py:772-816) is the direct title-lookup step that supplies candidate `related_notes` for the *first two* DAG calls (extraction, resolution) — it never reads file content, only `Note.title`, matching proper-noun phrases against note titles. It does **not** feed the revision call directly (revision candidates come from `entity_resolutions` with `action="update"`, resolved earlier).
- Separately, `prepare_enrichment` also builds `related_notes` (search-hit list, title + short snippet only, not full content) that feeds the extraction and resolution prompts via `_render_related` (llm/prompts.py:281-284) — that path is cheap (titles only) and is **not** where the cost lives; the expensive full-file inlining is specific to the revision call (`build_revision_prompt`).

**Conclusion relevant to the user's actual request**: today there is no distinction at all between Compiled Truth and Timeline when building revision-call context — the code doesn't even parse them apart before sending; it sends the raw file bytes. Splitting so only Compiled Truth is sent would require either (a) parsing out the top section using the same `_H1_RE`/`_TIMELINE_HEADING_RE` logic `_merge_entity_note` already has, and sending only that, or (b) something that pre-compresses Timeline into the Compiled Truth text so nothing is lost by omitting Timeline. Note the load-bearing tension: `note-revision/SKILL.md`'s "read the existing note in full" instruction and the re-synthesis discipline ("union of what was already known plus new") were written assuming full-file visibility — the model currently uses Timeline content as part of what it's re-synthesizing from. If Timeline is dropped from context, any fact that lives *only* in Timeline (not yet promoted into Compiled Truth) becomes invisible to future re-synthesis, silently regressing exactly the kind of fact the project's "never silently rewrite/lose user knowledge" principle is meant to protect — this is a real design question, not just an implementation detail, and should be central to the plan.

---

## 5. `ModelTruncatedError` / `ModelContractError.truncated` and `_split_candidates_by_content_length`

**`ModelTruncatedError`** — `src/wakil/llm/client.py:26-42`:
```python
class ModelTruncatedError(ModelError):
    """The provider stopped generating because it hit max_tokens.
    ... callers can retry with a larger budget instead of re-prompting for the same length."""
    def __init__(self, max_tokens: int, partial: str):
```
Raised by both `AnthropicClient.complete` (line 101) and `OpenAICompatibleClient.complete` (line 150) when the provider reports `stop_reason == "max_tokens"` / `finish_reason == "length"` (per `docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md`'s entry, dated 2026-07-20).

**Handling** — `complete_with_contract` (`src/wakil/llm/schemas.py:177-220`): one retry loop, `max_tokens = DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS` (8192) initially:
- `ModelTruncatedError` on attempt 1 → **doubles `max_tokens`**, resends identical prompt (truncation isn't a content problem, resending unchanged just truncates again at the same length).
- `ModelTruncatedError` on attempt 2 → raises `ModelContractError(schema.__name__, str(exc), truncated=True)`.
- `ValidationError` (malformed but not truncated) → attempt 1 appends the validation error to the prompt and retries; attempt 2 raises `ModelContractError(..., truncated=False)`.
- `ModelContractError.truncated: bool` (schemas.py:21-33) is the structured flag callers branch on — added specifically so `_revise_candidates` can distinguish "split and retry" from "this will fail identically on a smaller batch too."

**`_split_candidates_by_content_length`** (`ingest_service.py:1151-1171`) — greedy 2-way balance by **existing-note content length** (not entity count): sorts candidates longest-first, then places each into whichever running half currently has less accumulated content length, isolating the single biggest note from compounding with the next-biggest. Called from `_revise_candidates` (line 1228) only when `exc.truncated and len(candidates) > 1 and depth < _MAX_BISECTION_DEPTH` (`_MAX_BISECTION_DEPTH = 3`, line 1095, "caps worst-case fan-out ... to at most 2**3 = 8 sub-batches"). This is **reactive**: it only fires after a real truncation has already happened, discovering the safe batch size empirically per-run rather than precomputing one.

**ADR 0015** (`docs/adr/0015-relevance-gated-entities-and-truncation-driven-batching.md`) is the design document for exactly this mechanism, and is essential reading for the compression plan — summary:
- **Decision 1 (relevance gating, implemented)**: `EntityResolution.relevance: central|notable|minor|peripheral`, judged free during resolution; `_run_entity_updates` excludes `minor`/`peripheral` before the expensive revision call (`_LOW_RELEVANCE = {"minor", "peripheral"}`, line 1091), surfaced as a `proposal.warnings` entry, never silent.
- **Decision 2 (batching, Step A tried/rejected, Step B implemented in the uncommitted working tree — §0 above)**: Step A tested `output_config={"effort": "low"}` and `thinking: {type: "disabled"}` live against the Anthropic API to bound *thinking*-token cost (the actual dominant cost driver — 96% of consumed budget in the original failure was reasoning tokens, not output text) — neither worked (`effort` barely moved the needle; `disabled` broke JSON compliance outright). Step B (the bisection above) is therefore "the operative mechanism for whatever truncation risk remains after relevance filtering," confirmed necessary by a live re-run where even the 4 `central`-relevance survivors (including `people/edward-bridges.md` at ~32KB) still truncated.
- Explicitly frames this as reactive: "a size discovered empirically from an actual truncation is more defensible than one guessed at design time" — and explicitly rejects a fixed batch-size-by-count as a primary mechanism, and rejects clustering-by-topic (an extra model call) since every candidate already shares the same cached source-document prefix.
- Names the compounding cost driver a proactive compression mechanism would directly attack: **`companies/mosaic-private-markets.md` at ~53KB was, on its own, larger than the other nine targets combined** in the original failing case.

This is exactly the "reactive mitigation" you asked me to characterize precisely: it only kicks in after the fact (post-truncation), operates per-run (not persisted anywhere), and its unit of batching is the *candidate set for one revision call*, not the *stored size of an entity note*. A proactive "periodically compress entities" mechanism would complement it by keeping the notes themselves smaller so both the per-call context and the batching math stay cheap in the first place — it wouldn't replace Step B's role as a last-resort safety valve when a single note is still too large to send even alone (the ADR explicitly leaves that failure mode as "a real, surfaced failure ... not silently papered over").

---

## 6. Existing "compression"/summarization-adjacent code

**None found.** Grepped `compress|summariz|prune` and `truncat` across `src/wakil/**/*.py`:
- `_summarize_source` (ingest_service.py:497) — unrelated; builds a `SourceSummary` display object (id/title/status) for `wakil sources` CLI listing, not content summarization.
- `prune=...` occurrences (workspace_service.py, ingest_service.py, schema_migrate_service.py) — all about `index_notes(..., prune=...)`, removing stale SQLite index rows for notes deleted from disk, unrelated to entity-content pruning.
- `decompressed` (ingest_service.py:700, a comment) — about unzipping the vendored common-words wordlist, unrelated.
- All `truncat*` hits are exactly the `ModelTruncatedError`/`ModelContractError.truncated` machinery already covered in §5 — nothing else.
- `docs/entity-model.md`'s proposed `wakil entity compile <slug>` command (§3 above) is the closest existing *design* to a compression mechanism, but it's explicitly deferred/unimplemented and its own scope (re-synthesize Compiled Truth + Open Threads from all durable Memory rows) is about *promoting* raw content into synthesized state, not about *shrinking* an already-large Compiled Truth or Timeline for context-budget reasons — a genuinely new concern your planned mechanism would need to define from scratch.

**Conclusion**: there is no scaffolding, no half-built attempt, no stub function or TODO anywhere in `src/wakil/` for entity-note compression/summarization. This is greenfield.

---

## 7. Relevant ADRs (full list, `docs/adr/`)

| ADR | Status | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| 0001 skill-resolution-precedence-first-match-wins | — | Not directly relevant (skill file precedence rules), skipped in depth. |
| 0002 qmd-first-class-search | — | Search engine choice; not directly relevant. |
| 0003 git-native-change-tracking | — | Commits as the change-tracking mechanism; relevant only insofar as any compression write should follow the same git-commit-per-operation pattern other durable writes use. |
| 0004 exclude-live-model-skill-evals-from-default-ci | — | Establishes the norm that new *judgment* guidance (as opposed to deterministic code) needs a live-model eval, not just unit tests — cited repeatedly by ADR 0015 and directly relevant: any new "should this entity be compressed now" judgment would need the same eval treatment. |
| **0005 timeline-entries-as-memory-rows** | Accepted, partially implemented | Timeline entries should be `Memory` rows (`memory_type='event'`, new `event_date` column), reusing the existing lifecycle rather than a dedicated `timeline_entries` table — but this reuse isn't actually wired into `apply_enrichment` yet (see §2). Directly relevant: any compression scheme that wants to reconstruct/verify Timeline content programmatically will currently have to parse Markdown text, not query structured rows. |
| 0006 backlinks-as-live-query-over-widened-relationship-table | Accepted | Backlinks (the "Referenced in [...]" bullets baked into Timeline text today) should become a live SQL query over a widened `Relationship` table instead of stored prose — relevant because any Timeline-preserving compression must not corrupt/lose these auto-generated bullet lines, which `note-revision`/`entity-enrichment` both call out as "never touched." |
| 0007 markdown-source-of-truth-sqlite-operational-store | Accepted | Compiled Truth content is Markdown-only, never stored in SQLite — git provides version/diff/revert history, deliberately avoiding a GBrain-style `page_versions` snapshot table. Directly relevant: a compression mechanism's "before" state is recoverable via `git log`/`git diff` on the note file itself, not a database table — any design should lean on that rather than inventing a new snapshot mechanism. |
| 0008 ingestion-decomposition-reject-multi-agent-mechanism | Accepted | Establishes the fixed classify/extract/resolve/enforce/finalize DAG (implemented as `prepare_capture`/`prepare_enrichment`/`apply_*` code, not agent-decided delegation) as the shape all ingestion work must fit, explicitly rejecting multi-agent orchestration per CLAUDE.md's design biases. A compression mechanism should likely be its own explicit DAG node or standalone command, not a new autonomous agent. |
| 0009 prioritize-context-referenced-notes-in-related-search | Accepted | `@file:`-referenced notes get privileged, non-relevance-gated inclusion in `related_notes`. Tangential; not directly about compression. |
| 0010 capture-time-title-and-abstract-generation | Accepted | One cheap model call at capture time generates title/abstract. Tangential — shows precedent for a cheap, separate, single-purpose model call outside the main enrich DAG (a compression command could follow this shape). |
| 0011 retire-schema-md-dependency / 0012 resolver-md-migration-strategy | Accepted | Migration away from the target-vault's own `SCHEMA.md`/`resolver.md` files toward wakil's own schema catalog (`src/wakil/schema/entities/*.yaml`). 0012 explicitly references entity-model.md's Compiled Truth/Timeline convention as one of the things being migrated onto wakil's own schema authority (line 124). Relevant as background on where the canonical page-shape definition now lives (in-repo YAML/templates, not the user's vault). |
| **0013 opinion-memory-type-and-confidence-ranking** | Accepted | Adds `memory_type='opinion'` as a free-string addition and repositions `confidence` as (also) a retrieval-ranking input, distinguishing observed fact from subjective interpretation. Not directly about compression, but establishes the `Memory` extension pattern (free-string type + new field) later reused by relevance (`EntityResolution.relevance`, ADR 0015) — a plausible template for whatever "should this entity be compressed" signal gets added. |
| **0014 memory-register-field-and-query-exclusion** | Accepted | Adds explicit `register: formal\|casual` field to `Memory`, excluded from query grounding by default (low-commitment "hot takes" shouldn't ground answers with full weight). Not directly about compression; same "new Memory field, new default-exclusion rule" pattern as 0013. |
| **0015 relevance-gated-entities-and-truncation-driven-batching** | Accepted, Decision 1 implemented + live-eval-gated as incomplete, Decision 2 implemented in the working tree (uncommitted) | Covered in full in §5. The single most load-bearing ADR for this project: names the exact failure mode (large existing notes → truncated revision responses), the reactive fix (relevance gating + truncation-triggered bisection batching), and explicitly notes the biggest cost driver observed (~53KB note) as evidence a proactive size-reduction approach would help. Also documents that lowering `thinking` effort/disabling thinking does **not** fix the underlying cost — meaning a compression mechanism that shrinks note *size* is one of the few levers actually confirmed to reduce request cost, as opposed to token-budget tuning which was tried and failed. |

I also grepped `docs/adr/*.md` for "compiled truth" and "context" directly — no ADR beyond 0015 (which discusses "the page's entire 'Compiled Truth' section, not just a diff" as the thing the revision call re-synthesizes) and 0007 (Compiled Truth storage location) mentions either term meaningfully; 0009's "context" hits are about `--context`/`@file:` CLI flags, unrelated to model context-window budget.

---

## 8. CLAUDE.md principles and any overriding per-directory guidance

**No nested `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md` files exist anywhere else in the repo** (`find` for both names, excluding `.venv`, returned only the root `/Users/ebridges/Projects/wakil/CLAUDE.md`) — nothing under `schema/` or `skills/` overrides or supplements it.

Principles from the root `CLAUDE.md` most load-bearing for a compression mechanism:

- **Design Biases → Prefer**: "clear memory lifecycle," "human review," "explicit commands," "small composable services."
- **Design Biases → Avoid**: "large agent frameworks," "hidden background behavior," "automatic rewriting without review," "multi-agent orchestration," "opaque memory systems."
- **Working Agreement for Agents**, items 9, 11, 12 are the most directly binding: *"Respect the distinction between raw sources, durable notes, and memory."* / *"Show reviewable diffs for knowledge-base modifications."* / *"Do not silently rewrite user knowledge."*
- **Prime Directive**: "Does this clearly improve local Markdown knowledge work for one user?" — gate for whether compression is worth building at all vs. e.g. just fixing the context-inclusion split.

These are echoed and reinforced everywhere in the skill/ADR layer already surveyed: `note-revision/SKILL.md`'s entire "clobbering bug" section, `docs/memory-model.md`'s "Where this meets wakil's principles" (explicitly: "Silent reconsolidation is exactly the thing wakil exists not to do... Anything that changes durable Markdown is a proposal surfaced for review, expressed as a diff, gated on confirmation"), and ADR 0015's own citation of CLAUDE.md items 11/12 as justification for surfacing relevance-exclusions as visible warnings rather than dropping them silently. Any entity-compression design should therefore almost certainly be: (a) an explicit, separately-invoked operation (not something that runs automatically inside `wakil enrich`), (b) diff-previewed and confirm-gated exactly like every other note write path (`apply_enrichment`'s stale-file re-read guard at ingest_service.py:1358-1375 is the concrete precedent to mirror), and (c) never destructive of raw evidence — git history (per ADR 0007) is treated as the durable safety net for "what did this note used to say," so compression can lean on `git log`/diff rather than needing its own undo mechanism, but the compressed *file* itself must not silently drop facts that live only in Timeline, per the tension flagged in §4.

1	---
2	title: Relevance-Gated Entity Selection and Truncation-Driven Batching for Entity Revision Calls
3	status: accepted
4	date: 2026-07-25
5	audience: wakil design
6	---
7	
8	# Relevance-Gated Entity Selection and Truncation-Driven Batching for Entity Revision Calls
9	
10	`status: accepted` means the design below is settled, not that all of it is
11	built: Decision 1 is implemented (pending its live-eval gate, see
12	Consequences); Decision 2 is not yet implemented — see its steps for what
13	remains.
14	
15	## Context
16	
17	The entity-revision DAG node (`_run_entity_updates` in `app/ingest_service.py`,
18	the third model call in ADR 0008's classify/extract/resolve/enforce/finalize
19	decomposition) batches every `action=update` entity-resolution result into a
20	single model call and asks it to decide, per entity, whether the source
21	warrants a real change to that entity's page — and if so, to re-synthesize
22	the page's entire "Compiled Truth" section, not just a diff.
23	
24	A real `wakil enrich` run against a Scorealytics planning-meeting transcript
25	touching 10 already-paged entities failed with a truncated response even
26	after `complete_with_contract`'s existing doubling retry (8192 → 16384
27	tokens) — a recurrence of a previously-documented failure mode
28	(`docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md`, "`EOF while parsing a string` ... may mean the
29	model response was truncated," 2026-07-20), whose original fix (detect
30	truncation distinctly, double the budget once) was a stopgap for surfacing
31	the failure clearly, not a structural fix for large batches.
32	
33	Diagnosing this run surfaced two separate, compounding problems:
34	
35	1. **Every existing-page entity a source mentions becomes an equally-weighted
36	   "update" candidate**, regardless of how central it actually is to the
37	   source. `entity-resolve/SKILL.md`'s original wording made this
38	   unconditional ("a page for this entity already exists ... a later step
39	   decides what, if anything, should change"). The resolution step's
40	   `confidence` field looked like it might already capture this, but
41	   checking a real run's output against the user's own relevance
42	   assessment of the same 10 entities showed a clean divergence: a company
43	   mentioned only once, in passing, as background context (the reason for
44	   a scheduling constraint, never itself discussed) scored `confidence:
45	   0.95` — indistinguishable from the meeting's actual participants —
46	   because `confidence` was answering a different question (identity-match
47	   certainty: "is this definitely the same Mosaic as the existing page")
48	   than relevance ("does this source actually concern Mosaic"). Neither
49	   the Pydantic field nor the skill file had ever defined what `confidence`
50	   was supposed to mean; nothing downstream used it beyond CLI display.
51	
52	2. **Batching many candidates into one revision call risks truncation, and
53	   the one failure observed so far doesn't cleanly indict a particular
54	   cause.** Only ~2644 characters (~660 tokens at a 4-chars/token estimate)
55	   of actual output had been generated by the time the 16384-token ceiling
56	   hit — meaning roughly 96% of the consumed budget went to
57	   `thinking={"type": "adaptive"}` reasoning, not the text the model was
58	   asked to produce. That rules out "the response text itself is too long"
59	   as the primary story. It does **not**, on its own, establish how thinking
60	   cost scales with what's in the request — with a single data point, "cost
61	   scales with entity count," "cost is a large fixed per-call overhead
62	   independent of count," and "cost scales with something else entirely
63	   (e.g. ambiguity of the has_update judgment)" are all still consistent
64	   with the evidence. Any batching or budget-bounding response to this
65	   failure is, honestly, a hypothesis to be checked against a rerun of the
66	   real failing case — not a conclusion the one incident already proves.
67	
68	## Decision
69	
70	**1. Separate relevance from confidence as two independently-judged fields**
71	(implemented; commit `a656537` on branch
72	`feat/entity-revision-caching-and-relevance`):
73	
74	- `EntityResolution` gains `relevance: central | notable | minor |
75	  peripheral | None`, judged by the resolution step from the same source
76	  read it already performs to decide `create`/`update`/`skip` — no
77	  additional model call. `confidence` gains an explicit field description
78	  constraining it to identity-match certainty, distinct from relevance.
79	  Both are defined with worked examples in `entity-resolve/SKILL.md`.
80	- `_run_entity_updates` excludes `minor`/`peripheral` candidates before the
81	  (expensive) revision call. Missing/`None` relevance is treated as
82	  inclusive by omission — a model that doesn't emit the field never
83	  silently loses an entity that should have been updated.
84	- Excluded entities are surfaced as a visible `proposal.warnings` entry
85	  ("N entities left untouched as below the relevance threshold: ...")
86	  rather than dropped without a trace, and the CLI's entity-resolution
87	  preview table gained a Relevance column alongside the existing
88	  Confidence column — reviewable before anything is applied, per
89	  `CLAUDE.md`'s "show reviewable diffs for knowledge-base modifications"
90	  and "do not silently rewrite user knowledge." This is the same
91	  visibility contract every other degraded-but-non-blocking outcome in
92	  this DAG already uses (a missing target file, a failed resolution call);
93	  it is not a new, weaker pattern introduced here.
94	- **Not yet done, required before Decision 1 is considered complete**: a
95	  live-model eval scenario for `entity-resolve/SKILL.md`'s new relevance
96	  guidance, per this project's own established norm (ADR 0004) that new
97	  judgment guidance — as opposed to deterministic code — needs live
98	  verification, not just schema-level unit tests. The only calibration
99	  this field currently has is the single case study that motivated this
100	  ADR; unit tests over `EntityResolution` check that the four Literal
101	  values validate, nothing about whether the model applies them the way a
102	  human would. `EntityResolutionOutput` is also a single call batching
103	  every mentioned entity into one response, and this field adds output to
104	  every entity in it — smaller than a full compiled-truth regeneration,
105	  but the same call shape as the one that failed, and not exercised by
106	  this ADR's fix. It is not brought into scope here (its failure mode has
107	  not been observed in practice, and its per-entity output is much
108	  smaller), but it shares the structural exposure Decision 2 addresses for
109	  the revision call, and should get the same treatment if it is ever
110	  observed to truncate.
111	
112	**2. Respond to truncation with a sequenced, evidence-gated set of fixes —
113	not a single mechanism adopted on the strength of one incident** (Step A
114	below has now been tried and ruled out; Step B remains proposed, not yet
115	implemented):
116	
117	- **Step A — tried, rejected.** `AnthropicClient.complete` (`llm/client.py`)
118	  hardcodes `thinking={"type": "adaptive"}` for every call, with no bound
119	  on how much of `max_tokens` adaptive thinking can consume before any
120	  output is produced. `thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` — a
121	  fixed cap in place of adaptive mode — is not viable at all: it returns a
122	  400 error on `claude-opus-4-8` (`DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_MODEL`) and every
123	  later model in the family, per Anthropic's migration guide
124	  (platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/migration-guide.md,
125	  "Migrating to Claude Opus 5 from Claude Opus 4.8" and "Migrating to
126	  Claude Mythos 5 and Claude Fable 5 from Claude Opus 4.8," fetched and
127	  confirmed live 2026-07-25). The two levers that are actually available —
128	  `output_config={"effort": ...}` and `thinking: {type: "disabled"}`,
129	  both confirmed real against the installed SDK's type definitions
130	  (`anthropic==0.116.0`) — were tested directly against a reconstruction
131	  of the original failing request (the same 10 entities, including
132	  `companies/mosaic-private-markets.md` at ~53KB and
133	  `people/edward-bridges.md` at ~32KB of existing content, ~68K input
134	  tokens total, `max_tokens=16384` matching the second/final attempt that
135	  originally truncated), replayed live against the Anthropic API. Results:
136	  - **Baseline** (`thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`, no `output_config`):
137	    completed without truncating this run (`stop_reason: end_turn`), but
138	    consumed 16,296 of 16,384 output tokens (99.5%), 10,168 of them
139	    thinking — confirming the batch genuinely operates at the edge of the
140	    budget, even without directly reproducing a truncation on this
141	    particular run (target-note content has likely drifted since the
142	    original incident via unrelated later enrichments, so an exact replay
143	    wasn't possible).
144	  - **`output_config={"effort": "low"}`**: 10,111 thinking tokens — a
145	    0.6% change from baseline. **Effort does not meaningfully control
146	    adaptive-thinking cost for this call shape.** The hypothesis that
147	    lowering `effort` reduces the dominant cost driver is not supported by
148	    this data.
149	  - **`thinking: {type: "disabled"}`**: avoided the budget crunch entirely
150	    (8,589 of 16,384 output tokens, comfortable margin) — but the response
151	    was not valid JSON. Without a dedicated thinking channel, the model
152	    reasoned in plain prose directly in the text response ("Let me work
153	    through each...") instead of emitting the required schema, violating
154	    "respond with a single JSON object and nothing else." This is a hard
155	    contract failure (the same practical outcome as `ModelContractError`),
156	    not a quality tradeoff, and it occurred despite having budget to
157	    spare — disabling thinking doesn't trade cost for quality here, it
158	    breaks structured output outright.
159	
160	  **Neither lever is a viable fix.** `effort` doesn't touch the actual
161	  cost driver; `disabled` avoids the token-budget problem but reliably
162	  produces an unusable response for this task shape. Step A does not
163	  reduce what Decision 2 needs to solve. This makes Decision 1's
164	  relevance filtering more load-bearing than originally framed, not less:
165	  it independently removes the single largest cost driver in this batch
166	  (Mosaic's ~53KB note, correctly judged `peripheral`) without touching
167	  `thinking` at all, and Step B is the mechanism actually available for
168	  whatever risk remains after that filtering.
169	- **Step B — confirmed necessary, not yet implemented.** Re-running the
170	  original failing source through the actual `wakil enrich` command with
171	  Decision 1 (relevance filtering) in place, on the real live pipeline
172	  rather than a reconstruction (2026-07-25): relevance filtering correctly
173	  excluded 6 of the original candidates (`Brian Corr`, `Jake McGuire`,
174	  `Prabhuddha Bhan`, `Murtaza Mister` as `minor`; `Mosaic`, `Scorealytics
175	  News Accuracy Framework` as `minor`/`peripheral`) — but the remaining
176	  batch of 4 `central` entities (Lawrence Krubner, Edward Bridges,
177	  Scorealytics, Scorealytics AI Mentoring Program — still including
178	  `people/edward-bridges.md` at ~32KB) **still truncated**, at the same
179	  `max_tokens=16384` ceiling, after only 3,783 output chars. Relevance
180	  filtering reduced the problem; it did not eliminate it. Batch adaptively
181	  rather than by a precomputed size, on the reasoning that thinking-token
182	  cost is not reliably predictable from the request ahead of time (see
183	  Context #2), so a size discovered empirically from an actual truncation
184	  is more defensible than one guessed at design time:
185	  - Attempt the full relevance-filtered candidate set as **one** revision
186	    call — the common case after relevance filtering is already small
187	    (single digits for one source), so this costs nothing extra when
188	    batching isn't needed.
189	  - If the call still truncates after `complete_with_contract`'s existing
190	    doubling retry, split the candidate set and retry each half as its own
191	    call, recursively. The split point is chosen by existing-note content
192	    length (the batch's single largest note is isolated into its own half
193	    first), not blind index order — content length is a real, computable
194	    proxy for output cost even though it isn't the whole story, and using
195	    it to choose *where* to cut is a cheap, targeted use of that signal
196	    even though it was rejected as the trigger for *whether* to cut (see
197	    Alternatives Considered).
198	  - **Hard ceiling, not unbounded recursion**: a fixed maximum recursion
199	    depth (proposed: 3, i.e. at most 8 sub-batches from one original call)
200	    caps worst-case latency and API cost for a single `wakil enrich`
201	    invocation. A batch that still fails at the depth limit surfaces as a
202	    real, visible failure for its remaining entities — not further split,
203	    not retried indefinitely.
204	  - Every sub-call reuses the same `system` prompt and `cacheable_prefix`
205	    (source document + context + extraction summary — landed alongside
206	    relevance filtering, commit `6b64a5a`), so a split costs the
207	    incremental per-entity tokens, not a full-price repeat of the shared
208	    content.
209	  - Requires `ModelContractError` to preserve *why* it failed (truncation
210	    vs. a schema-validation failure) — only truncation justifies a split;
211	    a validation failure would recur identically on a smaller batch for an
212	    unrelated reason. Today the distinction is only embedded in the
213	    exception's string message, not a structured attribute callers can
214	    branch on. This prerequisite, and the bisection logic itself, are
215	    deterministic control flow — testable with a fake `ModelClient` that
216	    scripts a `ModelTruncatedError` sequence, the same pattern already
217	    used in `tests/unit/test_llm_schemas.py`. This does not need a live-
218	    model eval the way Decision 1's judgment field does; what it does need
219	    is validation against the real originally-failing transcript (or an
220	    equivalent fixture reproducing the same shape) before being considered
221	    proven, not just unit-tested in the abstract.
222	
223	## Alternatives considered
224	
225	- **Bound the thinking budget directly instead of working around it.**
226	  Tried and rejected — see Step A of Decision 2 above. `budget_tokens` is
227	  unavailable on this model; the two levers that are available (`effort`
228	  reduction, disabling thinking) were tested live against a reconstruction
229	  of the original failing request and neither works (`effort` doesn't
230	  meaningfully change thinking-token cost; disabling thinking breaks JSON
231	  compliance). This was the most direct response to the diagnosis in
232	  Context #2 (adaptive thinking, not output text, consumed the budget),
233	  and testing it before building batching complexity was the right call —
234	  it just didn't pan out. Listed here for visibility since an earlier
235	  draft of this ADR omitted it entirely from the alternatives it weighed,
236	  despite targeting the named root cause more directly than anything else
237	  discussed.
238	- **A dedicated LLM call to cluster candidates into topically-related
239	  batches.** Rejected: every surviving candidate already comes from the
240	  same source document, and every batch already receives that full
241	  document as the cached prefix — there is no missing cross-entity context

243	  latency to re-derive something already available for free.

245	  primary mechanism: a single failure at n=10 doesn't establish that any
246	  particular smaller number is safe, and Decision 2's own diagnosis

248	  against trusting a number picked without measurement just as much as it

251	  picked without measurement is exactly the kind of arbitrary guess this

253	  from an actual truncation rather than a precomputed count.

255	  as the thing that decides *whether* to split — the observed failure
256	  shows thinking, not output text, was the dominant cost, so content
257	  length alone would be calibrated against the wrong variable for that

259	  once a split is already needed (Step B): a real, computable proxy for
260	  output cost that costs nothing extra to use, since the content is
261	  already read into memory before the call is made.
262	
263	## Consequences
264	
265	- Enrichment runs skip real model work for entities the source doesn't
266	  substantively concern, at zero added model calls — the relevance
267	  judgment piggybacks on a call that already has to read the source.
268	- No entity's fate is decided silently: every relevance-based exclusion is
269	  visible in `proposal.warnings` and the CLI preview before `wakil enrich`
270	  writes anything.
271	- Decision 1 is not considered complete until it has a live-model eval
272	  scenario calibrating the new `relevance` judgment, matching this
273	  project's own norm for judgment-guidance changes (ADR 0004). Until that
274	  exists, the field's real-world accuracy rests on one case study, not a
275	  verified pattern — and run-to-run inconsistency has already been
276	  observed directly, not just theorized: the same source, re-resolved
277	  2026-07-25, rated Brian Corr `minor` where the case study that motivated
278	  this ADR rated the same mention "very relevant" (`central`). This
279	  doesn't invalidate the mechanism (the field still correctly identified
280	  Mosaic as low-value both times), but it's concrete evidence the
281	  judgment isn't perfectly stable, strengthening rather than weakening the
282	  case for the eval gate above.
283	- Decision 2's steps were ordered by directness and cost, gated on
284	  measuring each against the real originally-failing transcript before
285	  being adopted — that measurement happened (2026-07-25, see Step A) and
286	  Step A did not pan out: neither available lever fixes the problem,
287	  one of them (disabled thinking) actively breaks structured-output
288	  compliance. Step B is therefore the operative mechanism for whatever
289	  truncation risk remains after Decision 1's relevance filtering, not a
290	  fallback that might prove unnecessary.
291	- Decision 1's relevance filtering is now confirmed, independent of the
292	  Step A result, to remove real cost: in the reconstructed failing
293	  request, one excluded entity (`companies/mosaic-private-markets.md`,
294	  judged `peripheral`) carried ~53KB of existing content — more than the
295	  other nine targets combined. Filtering it out doesn't just reduce entity
296	  *count*, it removes the single largest driver of expected output size
297	  from the batch entirely.
298	- Revision-call count becomes variable per run instead of fixed at one
299	  once Step B lands, bounded by a fixed recursion-depth ceiling (proposed:
300	  3) rather than unbounded — most enrichments still cost exactly one call;

302	  number of extra calls, not an open-ended fan-out. "Bounded" is not
303	  "small": depth 3 with per-node doubling retry means a worst-case run can
304	  still cost on the order of 15-30 model calls. The ceiling caps the
305	  failure mode, it is not a latency guarantee.
306	- The relevance-threshold warning this ADR introduces (Decision 1) differs
307	  from the DAG's existing `proposal.warnings` uses in one respect worth
308	  naming honestly: the existing cases (a missing target file, a failed
309	  resolution call) are anomaly signals that fire rarely, so a user has
310	  reason to read one when it appears. This warning is expected to fire
311	  routinely — most sources touching several tangential entities will
312	  produce one on every run — which is a faster path to it becoming
313	  background noise a user learns to skim past. This is a known, accepted
314	  UX risk, not something this ADR resolves; its long-term visibility to
315	  the user hasn't been validated.
316	- `ModelContractError` needs a structured way to distinguish truncation
317	  from validation failure before Step B can be implemented safely; this is
318	  a prerequisite, not yet done, and is testable deterministically (a
319	  scripted fake client), not a live-model concern.
320	- This does not eliminate truncation risk outright: a single entity whose
321	  own existing note is large enough to overflow the budget by itself, or a
322	  batch that still fails at the recursion-depth ceiling, is a real,
323	  surfaced failure (a warning naming the affected entities) — not
324	  silently papered over, and not infinitely retried.
325	- `EntityResolutionOutput` (the resolution call, one step earlier in the
326	  DAG) shares the same single-call-for-every-entity shape this ADR treats
327	  as risky for the revision call, and Decision 1 adds output to every
328	  entity in it. It is explicitly out of scope here — its per-entity output
329	  is much smaller (no full-note regeneration) and it has not been observed
330	  to truncate in practice — but that is a known, accepted gap, not an
331	  oversight: if it is ever observed to fail the same way, it should get
332	  the same sequenced treatment (direct fix first, bounded adaptive
333	  batching second), not a redesign from scratch.
334	
335	## Sources
